title: Surprise and Shine Apple iPhone event live blog begins now!
content:
Macworld





Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event might be the most anticipated iPhone keynote in 10 years. It all kicks off Wednesday morning, and like you, we can’t wait. So join us as we count down the hours and minutes to the big show with all the latest rumors, leaks, and guesses leading up to the big event on Wednesday morning at 10 am PT.
Surprise and Shine iPhone event: How to watch
You can watch the full keynote right here using the embedded YouTube link below or on Apple.com on your iPhone or Mac. The “Watch Now” tab in the TV app on the Apple TV will also show the stream live.






Surprise and Shine iPhone event: What we expect
Apple might have dubbed this the “Surprise” event, but we have a pretty good idea what Apple is going to announce Wednesday morning. Here’s what we expect to see:
iPhone Ultra: Apple is almost certain to launch its first folding phone this week. We’re expecting a passport-style design with a 5.5-inch cover display and a near-8-inch inner display when opened.
iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max: We expect a similar design with a faster chip and a better camera system, possibly including a variable-aperture lens for the first time.
Apple Watch Series 12: The latest Apple Watch update will reportedly be a minor refresh with a new chip, all-day heart-rate tracking, and maybe the return of a ceramic finish.
Apple Watch Ultra 4: Like the Series 12, the Ultra 4 is expected to be a minor refresh largely focused on a new chip tuned for Siri AI.
AirPods 5: Apple is rumored to be launching a new pair of low-end AirPods, but we don’t know much about them.
Smart home: It’s less likely that Apple’s rumored smart-home hub arrives at this event, but we could see an updated Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini.
Surprise and Shine iPhone event: Live blog


2 mins ago, By Roman Loyola
Surprise and Shine iPhone event: Podcast preview






On the newest Macworld Podcast, Michael Simon and Jason Cross talk about what to expect at Apple’s Surprise and Shine iPhone event. What iPhones will Apple release? How will John Ternus do in his first keynote as Apple CEO? And will there be a “One more thing”? Get ready for the event by tuning in to the podcast.

2 hours ago, By Michael Simon
Cases, cases everywhere
The iPhone Ultra doesn’t exist yet, but you can find cases all over social media. It’s worth noting that case manufacturers don’t get information from Apple ahead of events, but they pay very close attention to the rumors and some probably have their own sources in the supply chain. Are they real? We’ll know in just a couple days.

					
						

						Link copied
						

							SHARE
						


							


3 hours ago, By David Price
Surprise? What surprise?
Apple has given this week’s showcase the tagline “Surprise and Shine.” But what’s the big surprise? Apple’s September events are among its most predictable, almost always revolving around new iPhones and new Apple Watches, and sometimes new AirPods.
September 2025: iPhones, Apple Watches, AirPods
September 2024: iPhones, Apple Watches, AirPods
September 2023: iPhones, Apple Watches
September 2022: iPhones, Apple Watches, AirPods
September 2021: iPhones, Apple Watches, iPads
Is John Ternus going to spring a surprise in 2026? After asking this question on TikTok we’re unconvinced by the idea of an Apple alarm clock (sorry), but another reader’s proposal of a “tabletop Pixar light robot personal assistant with Siri” is a little more plausible. That sounds a lot like the rumored smart-home hub which Apple has been working on for years, and could make an appearance this week. It could even turn up as One More Thing at the end and make for a fun encore.
But ultimately the most likely outcome is that, as far as Apple is concerned, the widely expected foldable iPhone counts as the surprise. To those of us who live in the Apple rumor bubble the iPhone Ultra (or iPhone Fold) now looks like virtually a sure thing for Wednesday’s presentation, but to the wider community it’s far less well known. And officially, of course, it doesn’t even exist. Surprise!

5 hours ago, By David Price
We (probably) know the new colors
Apple loves to launch at least one new color for each iPhone generation. Partly this allows the company to prune the colors which sold poorly the year before and experiment with alternatives, but the main advantage is that it allows customers to show off the fact they’ve got a new phone, even if the design is otherwise the same. Those who bought the iPhone 17 Pro in Cosmic Orange last year got some major bragging rights.
Perhaps surprisingly, the wildly popular Cosmic Orange is expected to be dropped from the range this year. The two new finishes are a little less garish: a dark-red/burgundy wine color, expected to be branded as Dark Cherry, and a light blue. Macworld exclusively revealed these colors in the summer.
If you’d like to see more of the new finishes, take a look at this leaked video, which appears to show demo models of the iPhone 18 Pro (in blue) and 18 Pro Max (in Dark Cherry).

iPhone pre-orders might start on Saturday
Generally, Apple opens up pre-orders for all the new iPhones and Apple Watches on the Friday following the Apple event at 5am PT. However, with 9/11 falling on Friday this year, it’s likely that Apple will delay the launch one day out of respect for the anniversary. Pre-orders instead are expected to begin on Saturday at midnight PT.

No iPhone 18 this week
In case you haven’t been following the rumors, Apple isn’t expected to launch a new iPhone 18 this week. That means the iPhone 17 will be on shelves alongside the iPhone 16 and 16 Plus for another six months. This would be the first time (other than the budget SE and e models) that Apple has spilt the new iPhones into separate launches and could create some serious FOMO for annual updaters.

title: High prices and no base iPhone 18 could hurt Apple but only in the short term
content:
Keybanc has historically had an Apple stock price target below reality, and its latest commentary about a lack of a non-Pro iPhone debut on Wednesday ignores a few key factors.


Mockup of a possible iPhone 18 Pro Max, which is rumored to come in a dark cherry red.
When Apple launches its new iPhones on September 9, 2026, it's expected to make two key changes. As well as the predicted announcement of a foldable iPhone Ultra, Apple is not believed to be launching its usual base iPhone models until spring 2027.
According to KeyBanc, these two factors present a potentially serious problem because it may lead investors to focus on the short term. That means them seeing that the models being launched are more expensive than before, and there's no lower-end iPhone to capture that market.

title: Apple TV's dystopian drama 'Silo' could live on with a rumored spinoff
content:
A rumored "Silo" spinoff could keep Apple TV's dystopian franchise alive beyond its planned finale, but the books' author is pushing back on the claim.


Image Credit: Apple TV
"Silo" is a dystopian science-fiction drama about a society living underground after humanity has been driven from the surface. The Apple TV series is based on the bestselling "Silo" trilogy, "Wool," "Shift," and "Dust," by Hugh Howey.
While it was well liked, Apple TV had told the creators that the series would end after the fourth season. The third season just returned to the small screen in July, with the fourth season anticipated to release in Summer 2027.

content:

title: This 13-in-1 Anker dock solves all of your cable problems and it’s 25% off
content:
Macworld





		
Anker Nano 13-in-1 docking station
View Deal
If your desk turns into a cable jungle every time you sit down to work, the Anker Nano docking station is for you. The best part is that it’s a two-in-one design that also gives you a portable hub to take with you when you work elsewhere. This 13-in-1 model is usually $150, but it’s down to $112 right now. 
For daily work, this hub gives you everything you could need. A single USB-C cable connects it to your laptop and gives you access to a bunch of ports. The front of the device houses a 10Gbps USB-C, a 5Gbps USB-C, a USB-A, an audio jack, as well as microSD and SD card slots. Then, on the back of the dock, there are two HDMI and DisplayPort, two USB-A ports, and an Ethernet port.
For whenever you’re out and about, you can take the 6-in-1 hub with you. The card slots, USB-A and USB-C ports on the front pop out, revealing another HDMI, USB-C PD port, and another USB-C Upstream port on the back. No need to buy a separate travel adapter—it’s already built in.
You do have to keep in mind that when paired with a Mac, multiple external displays run in mirrored mode only. Windows laptops get the full multi-monitor experience. But for $112, this Anker Nano laptop docking station is an easy pick if you want one hub for both your home office and life on the go.

title: iPhone Ultra: Latest foldable iPhone release date, price, specs and rumors
content:
Macworld





We’ve been reporting on the supposedly imminent launch of a foldable iPhone for years. There have been strong and reliable rumors of a foldable iPhone being just two years away, dating as far back as 2018, at least. Back then, reliable reports from the likes of CNBC said Apple was going to have a folding iPhone on the market in 2020.
That became 2021, 2022, 2024, 2025… and now it’s expected to land in 2026 – yes, this year! The wait may finally be nearly over: Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone on September 9 alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, although reports suggest supplies could be limited and some buyers may have to wait longer to get one.
Rumors suggest the new model could be called the iPhone Ultra and adopt a book-style design that opens into something resembling a small iPad. It’s expected to have an approximately 7.7- to 7.8-inch internal display and a 5.3- to 5.5-inch outer screen, with a wide 4:3 aspect ratio when unfolded. Apple is also said to have focused heavily on making the display crease as unobtrusive as possible while keeping the device exceptionally thin.
Inside, we’re expecting some variation of Apple’s A20 chip, around 12GB of RAM, Apple’s C2 cellular modem and potentially the biggest battery yet fitted to an iPhone. Camera rumors point to two 48MP rear cameras and two selfie cameras, but there could be some surprising compromises: the iPhone Ultra may ditch both Face ID and a telephoto camera, using Touch ID in the side button instead. And all that folding technology won’t come cheap, with current estimates putting the starting price at around $1,999 and potentially as high as $2,399 for the top configuration.
Folding iPhone rumors at a glance
Expected launch date: September 9, 2026, but limited supply possible
Likely name: iPhone Ultra rather than iPhone Fold
Form factor: Book-style, opening to a landscape view about the size of an iPad mini
Display: 7.7–7.8-inch inner display, approx 5.3–5.5-inch outer
Camera: Four cameras, no telephoto
Color options: Indigo and white/silver


What will the foldable iPhone be called?
iPhone Ultra is the expected name
Apple’s first foldable iPhone has long been referred to unofficially as the iPhone Fold, some may even refer to it as the iPhone 18 Fold, but more recent reports suggest the company may launch it as the iPhone Ultra.
In March 2026, Mark Gurman at Bloomberg reported that the folding iPhone would be one of several new products positioned in Apple’s “Ultra” tier. A month later, Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station (which is hit-and-miss) also claimed Apple was considering the iPhone Ultra name.
The strongest indication came more recently, when Gurman wrote on X that “everyone calls it the Ultra internally.” That makes iPhone Ultra the leading candidate, although it remains possible that “Ultra” is simply an internal name rather than the final branding.
Not everyone is convinced the name fits. Analyst Max Weinbach (to whom Gurman was responding with the above tweet) has argued that the foldable does not seem like an “Ultra” product in the same sense as Apple’s other highest-end devices. 


Everyone calls it the Ultra internally. We’ll see what happens.
— Mark Gurman (@markgurman) August 11, 2026





Alternative names floated over the years include iPhone Fold, iPhone Ultra Fold, iPhone Duo, iPhone Passport, iPhone Folio and iPhone Wide. The “Passport” nickname refers to the device’s reportedly wide, passport-like proportions when folded.
As of September 2026, however, iPhone Ultra looks like the most credible name. Apple has yet to confirm it, so the final branding may be one of the few surprises left for its “Surprise and Shine” event on September 9.


						

							


When will the foldable iPhone launch?
September 9, 2026 launch at Apple Event expected; retail availability may follow later
Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone at its “Surprise and Shine” event on September 9, 2026, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. The regular iPhone 18, 18e or iPhone Air 2, are instead expected to arrive in spring 2027.
There have been conflicting reports about when the foldable will actually go on sale. Nikkei Asia reported that Apple was running behind schedule, but Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman subsequently said the device was still on track, and could ship at the same time as, or soon after, the iPhone 18 Pro models. Barclays analyst Tim Long has been more cautious, suggesting the foldable may not ship until December.
There is also growing evidence in Apple’s software that the device is close. In June, product designer and engineer Sam Henri Gold found references in the iOS 27 framework to variables named “foldState” and “angleDegrees,” apparently designed to tell apps whether a device is folded and at what angle. Macworld independently confirmed those findings.


iOS 27 framework references “foldState” and “angleDegrees” but I’m sure that’s nothing pic.twitter.com/PcYNVvymms
— sam henri gold (@samhenrigold) June 8, 2026





Even if the iPhone Ultra launches on September 9, availability could be tight. During Apple’s Q3 earnings call, Apple then-CEO Tim Cook warned that that the impact of supply constraints would “increase significantly.” That raises the possibility that Apple could have limited stock initially, or begin shipping it later than the iPhone 18 Pro models.


						

							


What are the biggest trade-offs for the folding iPhone Ultra
Despite its expected “Ultra” branding and a price that could reach $2,000–$2,500, Apple’s first foldable iPhone may involve several compromises compared with the iPhone 18 Pro Max.
The biggest could be Face ID. Reports suggest the foldable will use a side-mounted Touch ID sensor instead, likely because its unusually thin design leaves less room for Apple’s TrueDepth hardware.
It may also sacrifice some camera capability. The foldable is not expected to include a dedicated telephoto camera, meaning buyers could miss out on the optical zoom available on Apple’s Pro models. That would be a significant omission on such an expensive iPhone.
The hinge also means Apple cannot use the same unibody-style construction as on a conventional iPhone, potentially affecting durability and dust resistance. The device is also expected to be eSIM-only worldwide.
There have been questions over MagSafe and wireless charging, partly because of the unusual construction of the rear casing, although more recent reports suggest MagSafe may ultimately be included.
Finally, the foldable is expected to run a specially adapted version of iOS rather than iPadOS. Its larger internal display should enable improved multitasking, but it may still fall short of the more desktop-like productivity experience available on an iPad.
Taken together, those compromises mean the iPhone Ultra could offer something genuinely new without necessarily being the most fully featured iPhone Apple sells. For some buyers, the iPhone 18 Pro Max may remain the more complete flagship.

				
					

				
			
The folding iPhone will reportedly have a Touch ID-enabled power button rather than Face ID.

Foundry



							


What will the folding iPhone look like? How will it fold? 
Book-like design with a vertical fold rumored
Intended to be an iPhone/iPad hybrid
Available in silver/white and Indigo Blue
Apple’s rumored iPhone Ultra is reportedly nearing mass production, with its design largely finalized. Here’s what current leaks suggest about how the foldable iPhone will look and how the hinge and display may work.
What color will the iPhone Ultra be?
The iPhone Ultra is expected to launch in just two color options: silver/white and dark blue.
Back in August, we reported that Apple was working on an Indigo option for its folding phone. Our sources also say that Apple does not currently plan to offer its first folding iPhone in black or space gray. The blue finish is expected to be particularly dark, reportedly closer to the iPhone 17 Pro’s Deep Blue than the MacBook Neo’s Indigo.
A subsequent leak shared by Sonny Dickson on Bluesky added weight to those reports, with photos reportedly showing camera protectors in silver and a deep blue shade that could resemble Indigo, Midnight or the iPhone 17 Pro’s Deep Blue.


These iPhone Fold camera protectors give us a look at two of the colors planned for the device: silver and dark blue.
— Sonny Dickson (@sonnydickson.bsky.social) 2026-08-08T22:44:44.846Z





The leaked camera protector matches previous design rumours, showing a horizontal rounded camera bar with openings for two cameras, a microphone and flash.
Book-style, iPad hybrid, design
Multiple leaks point to a book-style foldable with a large, tablet-like internal display, rather than a compact flip-phone design. The device is expected to function as a hybrid between an iPhone and an iPad.
This “passport-style” design will appear noticeably squarer than a traditional iPhone when closed. When unfolded, it’s rumored to resemble an iPad mini-like screen with a 4:3 aspect ratio, offering a more expansive viewing experience.
Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reported in 2025 that Apple’s foldable will adopt a dual-display setup, with a strong focus on achieving a near crease-free screen when opened. 
Other 2025 leaks, including reports from Digital Chat Station on Weibo, also point to a vertical, book-style fold where the left and right sides close together – similar to devices like the Google Pixel 9 Pro Fold and Samsung Galaxy Z Fold.
Dummy models shared by Sonny Dickson on X in April 2026, demonstrate this book-like form factor. 

				
					

				
			The latest leaks and dummy models show the wide “passport” design of the iPhone Ultra.
Sonny Dickson




Additional dummy unit images from tech YouTuber Vadim Yuryev, further reinforce this wide, book-like “passport” design. 

				
					

				
			Vadim Yuryev
In December 2025, this 3D image of the iPhone Ultra, based on leaked CAD files, was created by a hobbyist and shared on MakerWorld (now removed), also aligning with these design expectations. 

				
					

				
			Subsy/MakerWorld
However, alternative concepts have existed. In 2024, The Information reported that Apple had explored clamshell-style prototypes, where the device folds top-to-bottom, similar to traditional flip phones.
This design direction may already be influencing competitors. Our colleagues on TechAdvisor report that Samsung is developing a “Galaxy Z Fold 8 Wide” with a similar 4:3 aspect ratio, potentially positioning it as a direct rival to Apple’s iPhone Ultra.
How Apple is overcoming hinge design and crease reduction challenges
Adding a hinge to an iPhone introduces significant engineering challenges that Apple has spent years trying to resolve. While competitors have released multiple generations of foldables, Apple’s slower entry to the market is widely attributed to its focus on refining the hinge and delivering a more seamless user experience.
The biggest technical challenge is the visible and tactile crease where the screen folds. Apple has reportedly made this a priority, aiming to minimise it to the point of being nearly imperceptible.
Weibo leaker Instant Digital claims the iPhone Ultra’s internal design will make it the most repairable folding phone on the market, with elegant modular and stacked elements that minimize interconnects and ribbons.
As a result, the hinge is expected to be a defining feature of the iPhone Ultra, combining advanced materials and engineering to deliver a smoother, more durable folding experience.
To maintain both thinness and durability, Apple is reportedly testing high-end materials for the hinge:
Titanium alloy (rumored for structural strength)
LiquidMetal, according to Ming-Chi Kuo (March 2025), for improved durability, better screen flatness, and reduced creasing.
In July 2025, Kuo reported that Apple had developed a method to reduce crease visibility using metal support plates to better distribute and control bending stress. Apple may use this “laser-drilling metal plate technology” rather than conventional etching to create a more precise microstructure. 
Apple also holds several patents for foldable mechanisms which, along with several rumored technologies, may be used:
Variable Thickness Glass: A key part of Apple’s approach is said to involve variable thickness display glass, which is thinner at the fold point to reduce stress during repeated use. This is expected to work alongside an optically clear adhesive layer, designed to further minimise strain and help prevent the visible crease that commonly develops in foldable devices over time.
Stress-Reducing Adhesive: An optically clear adhesive designed to reduce strain on the display during folding.
Ultra-Thin Profile: Expected thickness of around 4.5mm unfolded and 9.5mm folded.
Internal Support: Metal plates beneath the display to maintain a completely flat surface when opened.
In March 2026, reports suggested that Samsung Display – Apple’s primary screen supplier – has developed a near-creaseless OLED panel, showcased at CES 2026 specifically to meet Apple’s standards.


						

							


How big will the foldable iPhone Ultra be?
Approx. 9.5mm thick when folded
Approx. 4.5mm when unfolded
According to Jon Prosser in December 2025, Apple’s foldable iPhone Ultra could measure around 9.5mm when closed and just 4.5mm when open. For context, the iPhone 16 Pro Max is 8.5mm thick, while the iPhone Air measures 5.6mm.
If accurate, this would make the iPhone Ultra one of the slimmest foldables, highlighting Apple’s focus on minimising bulk despite the hinge.
However, when asked about the thickness of the iPhone Ultra in April 2026, YouTuber Vadim Yuryev said it would be “exactly 11mm”, which is larger than Prosser’s prediction. He also claimed it would be 0.36mm taller and 0.39mm wider than the iPhone 17 Pro. 
Other design features
A leak from Weibo account Instant Digital in February 2026 indicates the volume buttons will be on the top edge, aligned right.


						

							


How big will the iPhone Ultra screens be?
The iPhone Ultra is widely expected to feature:
Approx. 7.7–7.8-inch internal display
Approx. 5.3–5.5-inch external display
Ming-Chi Kuo (2025) and TrendForce (July 2025) both pointed to a 7.8-inch inner and 5.5-inch outer display, while The Information later suggested slightly smaller sizes of 7.7 inches and 5.3 inches. This suggests Apple may still be refining final dimensions.
However, a December 2025 report from The Information slightly revised these figures to 7.7 inches internally and 5.3 inches externally, indicating that Apple may still be fine-tuning the final dimensions.
When unfolded, the device is expected to feature a 4:3 aspect ratio, aligning it more closely with the iPad and reinforcing its positioning as a productivity-focused, hybrid device. This would be a notable departure from the tall, narrow displays seen in earlier foldables like the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold series. 
This wider layout is said to:
Improve multitasking
Enhance document reading and web browsing
Deliver an experience closer to an iPad mini


						

							


What specs will iPhone Ultra offer? 
A20 Pro chip, 12GB RAM, C2 modem expected
The iPhone Ultra is expected to use Apple’s A20 Pro chip, the same flagship processor tipped for the iPhone 18 Pro models. Supply-chain reports also point to 12GB of RAM and storage options reaching as high as 2TB.
Apple is also expected to use more of its own wireless silicon. That could include the C2 cellular modem alongside an Apple-designed Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chip supporting Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth. 256GB/512GB/1TB/2TB capacities are to be expected. 
One notable feature is MagSafe charging. In September 2026, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said the folding iPhone will support MagSafe, contradicting earlier reports that Apple might omit it because of the device’s unusual construction.
Battery capacity could be another headline feature. Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital has claimed the iPhone Ultra will have a combined capacity of around 5,000 to 5,500mAh, potentially making it the largest battery ever fitted to an iPhone.
That capacity may be split between the two halves of the device. References to “batteries” rather than “battery” found in the iOS 27 beta have fuelled speculation that Apple is preparing software support for a dual-battery folding iPhone.


						

							


What cameras will the foldable iPhone have?
The foldable iPhone is expected to use a dual-camera system on the rear, with two 48MP sensors arranged on a long, thin “plateau” similar to the iPhone Air. Reports suggest the camera bar will be black rather than color-matched to the rest of the phone.
There is still some uncertainty over the exact lens combination. More recent reports point to a wide and telephoto setup, while earlier rumors suggested Apple could omit the telephoto lens and instead use wide and ultrawide cameras. If the telephoto camera is missing, it would be a significant compromise for such an expensive “Ultra” model.
The foldable is also expected to have two front-facing cameras – specified to be the usual 18MP Centre Stage cameras by TrendForce in June – allowing one to be used when the phone is closed and another when it is unfolded. Leaks have suggested Apple could combine an under-display camera with a second punch-hole camera.
A November 2025 JP Morgan report also claimed Apple could omit LiDAR and optical image stabilization, although those details remain uncertain.
Not all the rumors point to cutbacks. Tech YouTuber Vadim Yuryev claimed in April 2026 that the camera sensors could actually be physically larger than those used in the iPhone 17 Pro. 


						

							


How much will the folding iPhone Ultra cost?
Premium price expected: $2,000 or more
Apple’s first folding iPhone is expected to sit at the very top of the iPhone lineup, with most reports pointing to a starting price of around $2,000.
Analyst Arthur Liao has predicted a price of up to $2,399, based on the high cost of components such as the folding display and hinge, as well as Apple’s usual premium margins.
A September 2026 TrendForce report puts the likely starting price at $2,099 to $2,299, with higher-capacity configurations potentially exceeding $3,000.
Reports from Weibo leakers have suggested a starting price of RMB 15,999 in China for the 256GB model, rising to RMB 19,999 for 1TB. Using the pricing relationship of comparable Apple products, that would broadly translate to around $1,999 to $2,399 in the U.S.
Taken together, the rumors suggest the iPhone Ultra will start at roughly $2,000, with higher-storage models costing considerably more.






FAQ
Why is Apple making a folding iPhone now?
If you’re wondering why Apple is only launching a folding iPhone now – years after Samsung introduced the Galaxy Fold in 2019 – the answer may lie in Apple’s long-standing approach to new product categories. Rather than being first to market, Apple often waits for a technology to mature before entering the space.
When Steve Jobs unveiled the original iPhone in 2007, he talked about how the rest of the market was constrained by physical keyboards and styluses, but the iPhone would instead have a multi-touch display that could change depending on the task. Apple may be taking a similar approach with foldables. The company appears to believe that display technology, durability, and consumer interest have finally reached a point where a folding iPhone could appeal to mainstream buyers rather than just early adopters.
In other words, Apple’s goal may not be to invent the foldable phone, but to make it a product that millions of people actually want to use every day.
Will the iPhone Ultra replace the iPhone Pro Max?
It is thought that rather than replace the Pro Max handsets, Apple will position the foldable as a new tier above it – similar to how the Apple Watch Ultra sits above the standard Watch lineup. That would allow Apple to maintain premium pricing without disrupting existing flagship models.
When will the foldable iPhone Ultra actually go on sale?
The folding iPhone is expected to be announced at Apple’s September event on Wednesday, 9 September 2026, but the phone may not go on sale for some time after that date. Reports suggest the device could go on sale sometime between October and December 2026.

title: Five iPhone 18 Pro Camera Features Seemingly Leak in Code
content:
Apple is working on a broader set of Camera app improvements in iOS 27 it has announced, according to a new deep dive from MacRumors forum member "pdfu."


‌iOS 27‌ beta code apparently points to five features that could arrive alongside new iPhone models this week or in a future software update:


Exposure scopes: The Camera app can display a waveform or histogram to help judge exposure while shooting. A histogram shows how much of the image is too dark, too bright, or in between, while a waveform shows similar information but keeps it lined up with where those areas are in the frame.

Focus peaking and highlight warnings: New code overlays helpful information right on top of the camera preview. Focus peaking highlights the edges of whatever's in sharp focus using a colored outline, while a separate overlay warns when part of the image is getting overexposed, using a solid color, a pulsing color, diagonal stripes, or a checkerboard pattern.

Repeated self-timer shots: Apple is adding the ability to take several timed photos in a row rather than just one. After each shot, the countdown starts again right away instead of waiting for the photo to finish saving, so the shots can be taken back to back.

Manual focus: A control for manually setting and locking focus, rather than relying on autofocus, has also turned up in testing, similar to what's already available in Apple's Final Cut Camera app. A version of this existed in iOS 26 with a focus slider, but that slider was removed in ‌iOS 27‌ beta 1. The underlying focus-locking code is still there, but Apple has restricted it to devices that ship with ‌iOS 27‌ or later, so it won't work on any current iPhone.

Aperture-based image correction: A change to how photos are processed could be tied to a future iPhone with a variable aperture, a lens opening that can widen or narrow rather than staying fixed. ‌iOS 27‌ can adjust lens corrections depending on the aperture setting, blending between up to four reference points to smooth out the results.
 

iPhone 18 Pro is widely expected to offer a variable aperture main camera suggests that at least some of the capabilities could arrive with the new models.

title: Leak Hints at Four New Features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4
content:
Ahead of the announcement of the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 later this week, code in the watchOS 27 and iOS 27 betas points to a series of new features for the product line.


The information comes from a new post from MacRumors forums member "pdfu." The findings include:


New "Readiness" app: An all-new separate Watch app referred to in code as "Readiness," distinct from the existing Vitals app. The ‌watchOS 27‌ launcher apparently includes it in the default Home Screen layout immediately after the Workout app, and the Watch companion app on ‌iOS 27‌ references the same app in its logic for arranging apps on the ‌Home Screen‌. Its name and placement next to the Workout app suggest Apple is preparing a more substantial readiness or recovery experience for the Apple Watch.

Richer strength workouts: Expanded health infrastructure to store individual sets, repetition counts, weight, equipment, body side, and duration.

New optical-sensing system: A new sensor family called "Sunstone4p0" with lower noise coefficients, and wrist- and orientation-based channel selection. This could point to revised heart-sensing hardware on an upcoming Apple Watch, featuring improved readings when the reflected pulse signal is weak and specialized sensing according to the watch's placement.

128GB storage: A NAND storage profile tied to the T8320 chip for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 suggesting that they could offer 128GB of storage, up from 64GB on previous models.
 

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported that the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 will tout new health and fitness features.

two unreleased game controllers in the first macOS 26.7 release candidate, identified by the internal names T6502 and T1057, and separately found evidence in audioOS 27 beta 8 pointing to a four-speaker HomePod surround sound system and a new "Party Mode" feature.

title: Xiaomi Announces Foldable iPhone Rival
content:
Xiaomi today officially announced the 18 Fold, its first wide-format foldable, at a product event in China, two days before Apple is expected to unveil its own first foldable iPhone.


The Xiaomi 18 Fold uses a similar wide-folding design to the Samsung Z Fold8 and Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone. It features a 5.38-inch outer display and a 7.58-inch inner display, both with 120Hz LTPO technology and 4000 nits of peak brightness. The display is protected by a new double-layer ultra-thin glass structure.

The phone folds around a redesigned hinge Xiaomi calls the "Dragon Bone" hinge, which the company says underwent 492 structural optimizations, facilitating a noticeably more rounded design than Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold8. It launches in four finishes, including a Nishino Red colorway and a limited Ceramic Special Edition capped at 1,500 units.

3nm process with a 10-core CPU clocked to 4.35GHz and a 16-core GPU. Xiaomi says the chip delivers a 60% multi-core CPU gain and an 85% GPU performance gain over its predecessor, with power draw down 25% and 64% respectively, alongside a dedicated NPU rated at 200 TOPS.

The rear camera system was developed with Leica and is led by a 200-megapixel main sensor, alongside a 50-megapixel ultrawide and a 50-megapixel periscope telephoto lens with 3.5x optical zoom. Apple's first foldable iPhone is expected to feature two rear cameras only, with no dedicated telephoto camera. 

The device ships with Xiaomi's HyperOS 4 software and a 6,000mAh battery supporting 67W wired and 50W wireless charging. Pricing starts at 10,999 yuan (approximately $1,638), for the base 12GB RAM and 256GB storage configuration, rising to 14,999 yuan (approximately $2,235) for the top 16GB/1TB model, with a limited Ceramic Special Edition at 15,999 yuan (approximately $2,384). Apple's foldable is widely expected to be priced above $2,000.

Xiaomi also introduced the Xiaomi Pad 9 Pro Max tablet at the event, which shares the Xring O3 chip, along with three electric vehicles under its Pengcheng brand. The company has not announced global availability for the 18 Fold; its earlier Mix Fold foldables have stayed exclusive to China.

own event on September 9 at Apple Park, where the company is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Event Could Hit Apple Shares, KeyBanc Warns
content:
Apple's September 9 iPhone announcement event could become a negative catalyst for the stock, KeyBanc Capital Markets warns.  


In a research note seen by Investing.com, KeyBanc said the event could motivate investors to weigh pricing decisions against the impact of higher costs on demand and margins. KeyBanc added that Apple faces a choice to either raise prices broadly to offset gross margin pressure, which could hurt unit volumes and trigger "sticker shock," or raise prices more selectively.

This could invite greater scrutiny of margins and raise the prospect of further price increases later down the line. The firm maintained an "Underweight" rating on Apple and a $250 price target, against a share price of $324.96 at the time of publication.

iPhone 18 lineup builds at around 80 million units across the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 and first quarter of fiscal 2027, down from roughly 91 million units a year earlier. The firm attributed most of the decline to the absence of a base ‌iPhone 18‌ model in this part of the product cycle, with higher pricing and a richer product mix expected to partially offset the lower volumes.

iPhone 18 Pro, raising it to $1,249, and a $200 increase for the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, raising it to $1,399. The firm expects the foldable "iPhone Ultra" to start at $2,199.

title: iPhone 18 Pro video leak appears to confirm blue and Dark Cherry color options
content:
Macworld





On Wednesday, Apple will hold a press event with the tagline “Surprise and Shine.” Officially we don’t know what products will be announced, but in reality we’re 95% sure the day’s reveals will include iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max handsets. And that number might have just gone up even further with the leak of a video showing demo models of the new phones.
A very brief video clip posted this weekend to the Naver platform appears to show two devices: an iPhone 18 Pro Max, and an iPhone 18 Pro. We can tell this partly because there’s a retail-style label in front of them, but also because they’re finished in colors that aren’t available as part of the current or recent iPhone range. In the video, one iPhone is a dark red/burgundy, the other a light blue, appearing to provide the strongest visual evidence yet for the iPhone 18 Pro colors exclusively revealed by Macworld.
The only other phone we see is a dark-blue iPhone 17 Pro Max, which the poster holds against the Dark Cherry 18 Pro Max for comparison.
The poster doesn’t offer much context for the video; the headline (via Google Translate) reads simply “iPhone 18 Pro Max Dark Cherry & 18 Pro Blue demo devices exposed” and the body text adds nothing further. But from the items in the background, including the aforementioned label, clear plastic stands, and security cables, it appears that we’re looking at a retail display for the new phones. Given how soon they will need to appear in stores, it’s plausible that outlets will have already received demo units, although it’s obviously risky for one to allow footage to leak online before the announcements.
We can’t guarantee that the video is genuine, and it wouldn’t be hugely difficult to fake footage of this sort. But there isn’t a strong reason to doubt it, and the evidence for these two colors is growing stronger with each passing day.
The iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, unless something very unexpected happens, will be announced at the event on Wednesday, starting at 10 a.m. E.T. Our iPhone event live blog is already up and running and will report all the breaking news and rumors as we find them.
And if you’d like to read the announcements before they happen… our crack reporters managed to get their hands on the script. Just don’t tell anyone, or we’ll get in trouble.

title: iPhone 18 Pro: Nine Reasons Not to Upgrade This Year
content:
Apple is set to unveil new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max models on Wednesday, September 9, and the devices are expected to feature a design that's largely similar to the iPhone 17 Pro models, with a peppering of enhancements inside. Major changes are not expected until next year, when Apple is expected to introduce a radically redesigned 20th-anniversary iPhone.


If you're thinking of trading in your current iPhone for this year's latest, consider the following features rumored to be coming to next September's iPhone 20 models (Apple is expected to skip the iPhone 19 for its commemorative edition). Taken together, they may just give you pause for thought.

  
A quad-curved, all-glass design: The display glass reportedly curves away on all four sides of the iPhone 20, concealing the metal frame during normal use for a borderless effect. Apple is said to be working with Samsung on an "equal-depth quad-curved" display to achieve the feat.

Advanced OLED technology: Apple is planning to use a brighter, thinner OLED panel for the 20th anniversary iPhone. Rumors suggest that Apple will adopt Samsung ‌OLED‌ displays with Color Filter on Encapsulation (COE) technology, which reduces the thickness of the overall display stack, and lets more light through to improve brightness while reducing power draw.

  
Under-display Face ID and camera: Apple is reportedly continuing to test hardware that would eliminate the Dynamic Island – the visible cutout – from the front of the device, with Face ID components moving under the screen and an under-camera display said to be in development. Whether the technology will be ready in time for a fall 2027 launch remains uncertain.

Custom Apple image sensor: Apple is said to be developing its own stacked image sensor to replace the Sony sensors it has traditionally used for the iPhone. Apple has reportedly already developed a working prototype. The sensor is said to use LOFIC technology, which would let each pixel store varying amounts of light and potentially reach up to 20 stops of dynamic range.

  
Solid-state buttons: Apple is said to be testing haptic replacements for the Side, Volume, Action, and Camera Control buttons. The buttons could be integrated directly into the device's frame, with no actual physical movement when pressed, yet retaining a tactile responsiveness.

  
A 2-nanometer A21 chip: The 20th anniversary models are expected to feature a second-generation 2-nanometer chip. With the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro models widely expected to debut the A20 Pro chip, the anniversary models would likely be powered by the A21 Pro.

  
Silicon anode battery: Apple is reportedly exploring a new battery technology that uses a silicon anode capable of storing more lithium ions per gram, potentially delivering longer battery life without increasing the physical size of the battery.

  
Mobile high bandwidth memory: Apple is rumored to be evaluating vertically stacked DRAM technology to improve memory bandwidth and boost on-device AI performance.

  
Two sizes: The two anniversary models could have a larger display size compared to this September's iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, which are expected to use 6.3-inch and 6.9-inch displays similar to iPhone 17 Pro models. In contrast, Apple is rumored to be prototyping a 6.4-inch display for the iPhone 20 Pro, and a 7-inch display for the larger 20 Pro Max.

With all that said, we're still 12 months out, and Apple's plans shift constantly behind closed doors, plus features this ambitious have a habit of slipping a year or two. Under-display Face ID in particular has been "two years away" for about five years now.

title: Intego ONE now protects your iPhone too – and there’s 50% off in September
content:
Macworld

Intego ONE Complete, the Mac security suite we reviewed earlier this year, has expanded to the iPhone with the new Intego ONE: VPN & Wi-Fi Security app. It gives Complete subscribers VPN protection, Wi-Fi security checks and an assessment of their iPhone’s built-in security settings at no additional cost.
This is not antivirus software for the iPhone. Instead, the app complements Apple’s existing iPhone security by concentrating on areas where users can still expose themselves to risk: insecure Wi-Fi, unprotected internet connections and important iOS security settings that haven’t been enabled. That distinction matters. iPhones are resistant to traditional malware because of Apple’s tightly controlled security architecture, but they aren’t immune from spyware, exploits, malicious websites, compromised accounts and other privacy and security threats.
The new iPhone app is available to new and existing Intego ONE Complete subscribers. Intego is also currently a Back to School promotion that cuts the price by 50% until September 30. Intego confirmed that you don’t need to prove you are a student to take advantage of the offer. 
Get Intego ONE – Complete Plan for Mac & iPhone – Back To School 50% off (expires Sept 30th)


What is Intego ONE?
Intego ONE is the successor to Intego Internet Security X9, combining Mac antivirus protection with additional security and maintenance tools. It’s currently our top recommendation in our Best Antivirus for Mac guide. 
It comes in three tiers:
Essential: Antivirus and firewall.
Advanced: Adds SmartClean.
Complete: Adds Intego VPN and now includes the iPhone app. 
Essential and Advanced remain Mac-only packages.
We’ve already reviewed Intego ONE Complete on the Mac, where its malware detection, scanning performance and firewall controls particularly impressed us. In our testing, it handled more than 130 malware samples extremely well and scanned more than two million files in around eight minutes.
Those Mac security features remain the main reason to consider Intego ONE. The new iPhone app broadens the Complete package.
$29.99 at  Intego (annual) 						
					


						

							


What does Intego ONE do on an iPhone?

				
					

				
			
Intego’s iPhone app
adds a VPN, Wi-Fi security checks and iPhone security monitoring, but not antivirus scanning.

 
The iPhone version of Intego ONE is essentially a combination of privacy protection, network security and security configuration checking.
There are three main elements.
Intego VPN
When you’re using hotel, café, airport or other Wi-Fi that you don’t control, Intego’s VPN can encrypt your internet connection.
The VPN was already included with Intego ONE Complete on the Mac, where it encrypts internet traffic, masks the user’s IP address and can help protect data when using public or unsecured Wi-Fi.
When we tested it as part of our Mac review we found it simple to use, with 51 server locations and good bandwidth and streaming performance, although it isn’t as fully featured as some dedicated VPN services.
Adding the VPN to the iPhone arguably makes the feature more useful, because your phone is much more likely to connect to unfamiliar Wi-Fi while you’re travelling or away from home.
Wi-Fi security checks
Intego can also check the security of the Wi-Fi network your iPhone is currently using.
The test takes around 10 seconds and reports on connection speed as well as any potential security issues it identifies. Intego told us that one of the main things it checks is whether the network is using strong encryption.
iPhone security check-up
The app can also inspect some of the protections already built into your iPhone and tell you whether they are enabled or being used.
Intego says its Device Check-Up can check whether:
A passcode is enabled.
Face ID or Touch ID is enabled.
Apps are permitted to track you.
The iPhone is running the newest version of iOS it supports.
Something has been changed that removes Apple’s security protections.
Screen recording is active.
The key benefit is not that Intego provides these protections itself. Apple already does that. Instead, Intego checks whether important security features are enabled and flags potential weaknesses.
Intego confirmed that its warning about changes that remove Apple’s built-in protections refers primarily to jailbreak detection. It does not generally treat MDM profiles as suspicious, since these are commonly used by businesses to manage and secure devices. Intego also told us that it plans to add Developer Mode detection in a future update, subject to the access Apple’s APIs allow.


						

							


But can an iPhone actually get a virus?
If Intego ONE is an antivirus suite, you might reasonably assume that its new iPhone app scans the iPhone for viruses.
It doesn’t.
Traditional iPhone viruses are extremely uncommon because iOS apps are sandboxed, Apple tightly controls software distribution and the operating system incorporates substantial security protections.
That doesn’t make an iPhone invulnerable. Spyware, security exploits, malicious websites, compromised accounts and other threats can still put personal information at risk.
Intego isn’t claiming to replace Apple’s malware protection. Its proposition is effectively this: Apple protects the operating system, while Intego helps with some of the connections and security decisions that remain under the user’s control.

This is the group that benefits most from the change. On the Mac you get the antivirus and firewall protection that impressed us in testing, alongside SmartClean and a VPN. On the iPhone you get the same VPN plus Wi-Fi security and device-security checks.

If you don’t own a Mac or don’t need Mac antivirus protection, a standalone VPN or other dedicated iPhone security service may make more sense. See our recommendations of the best VPN for iPhone. 


						

							


Does the iPhone app make Intego ONE Complete better value?

				
					

				
			
The Intego ONE iPhone app can be downloaded from the iOS App Store. 

 
Our Intego ONE review already recommended the suite for its strong malware detection, firewall, performance and ease of use, although we noted omissions including phishing protection and parental controls.
The new iPhone app doesn’t address those weaknesses, but it does make the Complete tier more useful for people who own both a Mac and an iPhone.
On the Mac, Intego ONE Complete includes antivirus, firewall protection, SmartClean and a VPN. On the iPhone, you get the VPN plus Wi-Fi security checks and tools that flag potentially important security settings. It isn’t antivirus for the iPhone and shouldn’t be confused with one.
For existing Complete subscribers, the iPhone app is a worthwhile addition at no extra cost. title: iPhone 18 Pro & Max: Release date, price, specs and latest rumors ahead of Apple’s event
content:
Macworld





The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to launch at an Apple event on September 9, 2026 featuring several cutting-edge hardware advancements, including the debut of Apple’s C2 modem, and a shift to a 2nm manufacturing process for the A20 Pro chip. 
Other key rumored upgrades include a smaller Dynamic Island with under-display Face ID components and camera improvements that may include variable aperture on the Pro Max and enhanced sensors.
Alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max Apple is said to be planning to launch the ultra-premium folding iPhone. However, in a change to the usual schedule, the company is expected to shift the launch of the iPhone 18 spring 2027 to keep the spotlight on the Pro series during its traditional September debut. 
Here’s a quick summary of what all the rumors and leaks say to expect from the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in 2026.


What are the biggest upgrades for iPhone 18 Pro & Pro Max
Unveiling at Apple’s September 9 event
Smaller Dynamic Island, potentially with some Face ID components under the display
Variable-aperture main camera
A20 Pro chip built on TSMC’s 2nm process
Apple C2 cellular modem
New N2 wireless/networking chip
Larger battery, particularly on the Pro Max
Simplified Camera Control
Revised, more seamless rear Ceramic Shield design
Possible 5G satellite connectivity
Likely price increase due to soaring memory and component costs
How is iPhone 18 Pro/Max different from iPhone 17 Pro/Max?
Split release schedule (Pro first, base later)
Smaller or modified Dynamic Island
Some Face ID components moving under-display
New C2 modem 
Camera experimentation (rumored variable aperture on Pro Max)


						

							




iPhone 18 Pro/Max vs iPhone 17 Pro/Max


FeatureiPhone 18 Pro/Max rumorsLikelihoodiPhone 17 Pro/Max

Launch dateSeptember 9, 2026Confirmed eventSeptember 9, 2025
Dynamic IslandSmaller designCredible rumorNo change since 2022 iPhone 14 Pro
Face IDSome Face ID components moving under the displayPossibleNo change since 2022 iPhone 14 Pro
ModemC2 modemCredible rumorQualcomm modem
CameraImproved aperture technology for rear. 24MP selfie camerasPossibleAll three rear cameras are 48MP, optical-quality 8x zoom. 18MP front camera.
ColorsDark Cherry, Light Blue, Dark Gray, SilverMacworld source confirmedCosmic Orange, Deep Blue, Silver
Camera ControlPressure sensing Credible rumorCapacitive/touch-sensing layer

 Comparing iPhone 18 Pro rumors to current iPhone 17 Pro






When will the new iPhones launch?
Apple has confirmed that it will hold an event on Wednesday, September 9, 2026, and new iPhones are highly likely to headline the event.
However, Apple is widely expected to change its usual release strategy this year. Multiple reports suggest suggest that only the premium models will arrive in September 2026: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and a new foldable iPhone Ultra. 
The standard iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e and a second generation iPhone Air are instead expected in spring 2027. If accurate, this would represent the biggest shake-up to Apple’s iPhone launch schedule in years, creating separate autumn and spring release windows.
Evidence in iOS 27 beta 5 adds weight to those reports. System files reportedly reference six unreleased iPhones: the iPhone 18, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2, and foldable iPhone Ultra. The references don’t reveal specifications, but they support the idea that Apple is preparing all six models while staggering their release dates. 
Availability could also be a problem. During Apple’s Q3 earnings call, then-CEO Tim Cook, now executive chairman, warned that the impact of supply constraints would “increase significantly.”
Apple is reportedly struggling to secure enough DRAM for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra, potentially limiting production ahead of launch. Processor wafers are said to be ready, but some are reportedly waiting for memory before they can be packaged and assembled.
That could leave the iPhone 18 Pro in short supply when it goes on sale, with longer shipping estimates possible. The lower-volume iPhone Ultra may be somewhat less affected.
Most likely: The iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max, and foldable iPhone Ultra will launch in September 2026, while the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2 will follow in early 2027.


						

							




What iPhones are coming in 2026?


iPhone 18 Pro/Max9 September 2026
iPhone Ultra9 September 2026
iPhone Air (2nd gen)Spring 2027
iPhone 18Spring 2027
iPhone 18eSpring 2027

 
The anticipated launch dates for the 2026-2027 iPhones.






What will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max look like and what are the color choices?
The design of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max is said to resemble the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max, but some changes are predicted.
One possible change, shared by a Weibo leaker in September 2025, is a “slightly transparent” ceramic shield section on the back of Pro models. This glass/Ceramic Shield area around MagSafe is now rumored to become more frosted and visually seamless. 
Macworld contributor Filipe Esposito reported that a trusted source had revealed one of the new colorways for the iPhone 18 Pro to be Dark Cherry, replacing the iPhone 17 Pro’s Cosmic Orange option.
Recent rumors claimed that the new phones will be significantly thicker than previous models, but all the evidence we have seen says that’s not the case, including case maker Otter Box confidently listing their iPhone 17 Pro cases as fitting the iPhone 18 Pro. Instead, we expect the body to have about the same thickness as the iPhone 17 Pro/Max but with a thicker camera bump area.
Another report suggests that the Camera Control on the side of the iPhone will be pressure sensing instead of a touch-sensing layer. This redesign is said to be aimed at reducing the cost and complexity.  
A recent ransomware attack against an Apple parts supplier included images from an iPhone 18 Pro “drop test” and other parts, and they corroborate prior rumors about the overall shape and design of the phone, which is broadly the same as the iPhone 17 Pro.
Other shades are said to include: Light Blue, Dark Gray, and Silver. There was also a coffee shade rumored (via Digital Chat Station). 

 
 @macworld.com 
iPhone 18 Pro colors revealed! #iphone #apple
 ♬ original sound – Macworld – Macworld 
  




As with the iPhone 17 Pro, there will be no black option, according to Instant Digital.
Screen sizes are expected to remain at 6.3 and 6.9 inches. The Pro models will also retain the wider three-camera raised plateau.
If you are hoping for a more dramatic redesign, the iPhone Ultra may have more appeal. Alternatively, you could wait for the 20th anniversary iPhone which is rumored to have a “radically different design“. Reports point to a curved, near-bezel-free display, possible solid-state haptic buttons, a thinner and brighter OLED panel, and potentially under-display Face ID and camera hardware coming in fall 2027.
Most likely: Design changes will be minimal, with the biggest visible differences limited to colors and subtle refinements.


						

							


What’s new with the iPhone 18 Pro/Max camera?

				
					

				
			
Eugen Wegmann




Apple may introduce variable aperture technology to the 48MP main camera on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max (potentially only the Pro Max), allowing mechanical control over light intake and depth of field. This has long been a perk limited to high-end professional cameras.
If the rumor (from Digital Chat Station on Weibo) is true, iPhone users will be able to mechanically control how much light reaches the sensor for the first time, allowing more control over depth of field and sharpness. This could elevate portrait shots by improving the applied depth of field effect, as well as minimizing overexposure.
Wider telephoto apertures on the Pro models should also result in better low-light performance.
For some time (since January 2025) Samsung has been said to be working on a new three-layer stacked camera sensor called ‘PD-TR-Logic,’ and this could appear in the iPhone 18 series. This image sensor is expected to enhance the camera’s responsiveness, while also offering advantages such as reduced photo noise, improved dynamic range. The main Wide camera sensor is expected to be larger than usual, which offers many benefits.
The front-facing camera may also get an upgrade beyond the rumored changes to the housing (as discussed elsewhere the selfie camera may be housed in a smaller hole-punch cut out, reducing the size of the Dynamic Island). The iPhone 17 generation features 18MP sensors for the selfie camera, but this may increase to 24MP in the next generation, according to leaker WhyLab on Weibo.
More megapixels would lead to improved video calls and better low-light performance. 
Most likely: Incremental improvements, with a new variable aperture feature on the Pro Max.


						

							


Will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max Dynamic Island or front camera change?

				
					

				
			
Britta O’Boyle




Apple hasn’t changed the Dynamic Island since the iPhone 14 Pro, but the iPhone 18 Pro may introduce some adjustments.
Some reports suggest Apple could move certain Face ID components under the display, allowing the Dynamic Island to shrink. This is not expected to mean that the entire Face ID system will be hidden beneath the screen. 
A report in December 2025 from Weibo account “Smart Pikachu” claimed that Apple was testing an under-display “micro-transparent glass panel” for some Face ID sensors. That could allow Apple to reduce the size of the Dynamic Island on the iPhone 18 Pro.
Later reports, however, suggest that full under-display Face ID is not expected yet. Instead, Apple may move only some of the sensors or emitters used by Face ID beneath the display, while other components remain visible within a smaller Dynamic Island.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has also reported that Apple plans to “shrink” the Dynamic Island on future iPhone models, adding weight to the idea that Apple is redesigning or relocating some of the components currently housed within it.
A spy shot published in March by noted leaker IceUniverse on X gives us a view of how much smaller the Dynamic Island could be.

				
					

				
			
IceUniverse/X




There have been conflicting claims that the position of the front-facing camera may also change: 
In December 2025 The Information claimed Apple will put the Face ID sensors under the display, and move the front camera to the upper left corner in a punch-hole design. This would make the iPhone 18 Pro/ Max the first iPhones with a front camera in the corner.
However, Prominent leaker account Instant Digital said on Weibo in January 2026 that front camera claim was based on a mistranslation, and only the infrared sensor moves under the display. Leakers ShrimpApplePro and Ross Young of DSCC corroborated Instant Digital’s claims.
Most likely: A smaller Dynamic Island, with some Face ID hardware moved under the display, rather than fully under-display Face ID.


						

							


Will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max display change?

				
					

				
			
Stephan Wiesend




Screen sizes should be consistent with the 6.3 and 6.9-inch displays on the current models, but reports suggest a massive jump in brightness from the current 1600 nits HDR and 3,000 nits peak. 
According to Weibo leaker, Instant Digital, Chinese supplier BOE has revealed that Apple is targeting unprecedentedly high brightness requirements for the display. The Elec corroborated this, claiming BOE is struggling with iPhone OLED production so panel orders have been shifted to Samsung Display.
Most likely: An increase in brightness is expected, but there are no details yet on the extent of the improvement.


						

							


How powerful will the A20 chip in the iPhone 18 Pro/Max be?
The iPhone 18 series is expected to use a new A20 chip, built on TSMC’s N2 (2nm) process. The move to a smaller manufacturing process should allow Apple to pack in more transistors, with TSMC claiming up to 15% better performance or 30% lower power consumption compared with its previous-generation technology.
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to get an A20 Pro variant. A September 2026 leak suggests the A20 Pro could feature a 7-core GPU, up from six cores in the A19 Pro, while retaining a six-core CPU with two performance and four efficiency cores.
Perhaps more significant is the rumored move to a 96-bit LPDDR5x memory interface, 50% wider than the A19 Pro’s 64-bit interface. Combined with possible clock-speed and architectural improvements, we estimate that GPU performance could rise by around 20–30%, benefiting local AI workloads, 3D games and other graphics-intensive apps.
The A20 is also rumored to use Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module (WMCM) packaging, integrating the RAM more closely with the SoC. That could improve memory bandwidth and latency, while potentially reducing power consumption.
Apple could also borrow ideas from its M-series chips, with speculation that the A20 may introduce higher-performance “super cores” similar to those used in the M5.
Most likely: A substantial underlying upgrade in performance, graphics and efficiency, although many of the improvements may be more noticeable in demanding games and AI features than in everyday use..


						

							


Will iPhone 18 Pro/Max battery life improve?
Apple works to make battery life as long as possible every year, especially in the Pro model iPhones. 
A July report claimed that the battery capacity of the iPhone 18 Pro Max will have a battery capacity of 5,235 mAh on the Nano SIM model and 5,425 mAh on the eSIM-only version. That’s about 6-8% more capacity than the current model. Further reports have puts the U.S. eSIM iPhone 18 Pro Max at 5,567mAh. 
The “Pro Max” variant of the iPhone gets a higher-capacity battery nearly every year, usually a couple hundred mAh more, thanks to better internal design and improving battery chemistry and manufacturing techniques. But battery life is a function of more than just battery capacity—the power use of the processor, display, and wireless radios all play an important point.
We think it’s likely the iPhone 18 Pro/Max will have higher-capacity batteries, and battery life at least as long as the iPhone 17 Pro/Max. But a significantly longer battery life is hard to predict.


						

							


Will connectivity improve (5G, Wi-Fi, satellite) with iPhone 18 Pro/Max?
C2 and N2 chip rumors. 
iPhone 18 Pro models are rumored to feature the second generation of Apple’s in-house 5G modem, the C2 chip. 
The C2 hasn’t launched yet, but it is expected to replace Qualcomm modems in at least some iPhone 18 Pro models. Qualcomm hardware may still be used in certain markets, depending on regional and carrier requirements:
Better power efficiency
Faster and more reliable 5G performance
Improved mmWave support
There are also reports that the new iPhone will gain full satellite internet support, expanding beyond emergency use. In October 2025, The Information claimed that Apple is gearing up to support 5G networks that are served from satellites. 
While the iPhone has offered satellite connectivity for emergency situations for years, if this rumor is true it would allow the iPhone 18 models to have full internet access via satellite, not just emergency services.
As of April 2026, Apple and Amazon have agreed to team up to provide future satellite service support. Early in April, Amazon announced that it had agreed to acquire Globalstar, who was the provider of iPhone and Apple Watch satellite connectivity (that merger is expected to close in 2027) So now iPhones and Apple Watches will now fall under Amazon Leo, Amazon’s satellite internet network.
The Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip is less certain. Apple debuted its N1 local networking chip in the iPhone 17 line, supporting Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread networking.
Earlier in 2026, analyst Jeff Pu said that the iPhone 18 Pro models will introduce a next-generation N2 chip, but leaks of a iPhone 18 Pro motherboard in July 2026 suggested Apple could retain the N1 for another generation. There is little information about what an N2 would add beyond the capabilities of the N1.
Most likely: An incremental upgrade to wireless performance, reliability and efficiency rather than a major new connectivity feature.


						

							


How much will the iPhone 18 Pro/Max cost?
With Apple increasing prices for Macs and iPads in June due to high memory and chip costs, and the iPhone 18 Pro models are also expected to become more expensive.
In August, Mark Gurman described iPhone price increases as “inevitable” as Apple faces rising memory and component costs. 
A roughly $100 increase may be the most plausible outcome. Google and Samsung have both raised flagship prices by about $100, potentially setting a benchmark Apple may be reluctant to exceed. That could put the iPhone 18 Pro at around $1,199 and the Pro Max at $1,299.
Apple could also absorb some of the higher costs itself. Recent warnings about pressure on gross margins suggest the company may accept lower profitability rather than pass the full increase on to customers.
More pessimistic estimates are higher. IDC has suggested increases of up to $200 for the Pro models, while analyst Jeff Pu has indicated that prices could rise by as much as $250 to $300.
The rumored folding iPhone could further reshape the top end of Apple’s pricing, with reports suggesting a starting price of $1,999 or more.
Most likely: A price rise of around $100 for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, although larger increases remain possible if component costs stay elevated.
Current pricing is as follows:


						

							






iPhoneiPhoneCapacity

iPhone 17 Pro MaxFrom $1,199256GB – 2TB
iPhone 17 ProFrom $1,099256GB – 2TB
iPhone AirFrom $999256GB – 1TB
iPhone 17From $799256GB – 512GB
iPhone 17eFrom $599256GB – 512GB

 




 FAQ 


1.
When is the new iPhone coming out?
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to be unveiled at Apple’s September 9, 2026 event, with preorders likely shortly afterward (estimates suggest September 12) and availability around mid-September (estimates suggest September 18). The standard iPhone 18, however, is expected to arrive in spring 2027.





2.
Will the iPhone 18 Pro have under-display Face ID?
Probably not fully. Current rumors suggest the iPhone 18 Pro may move some Face ID components beneath the display, allowing Apple to shrink the Dynamic Island. However, the complete Face ID system is not expected to go under-display yet.





3.
What chip will power the iPhone 18 Pro?
Apple is expected to use the A20 chip in the iPhone 18 Pro. 





4.
Is Apple changing its iPhone release schedule in 2026?
Apple is said to be planning to launch the Pro iPhone models, including a foldable iPhone in September 2026. The iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e may not arrive until spring 2027. 





5.
What camera upgrades are rumored for the iPhone 18 Pro Max?
Apple is rumored to be focusing on advanced lens technology and sensor improvements for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. One prominent rumor is the introduction of a variable-aperture system in the Pro Max.

title: Apple Plans to Squeeze More Revenue From the App Store, Report Says
content:
Apple is looking at further ways to monetize the App Store and increase the company's recurring revenue from the platform, according to a new report.


Writing in his latest Power On newsletter, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said that newly appointed Apple CEO John Ternus and services chief Eddy Cue are behind the effort to raise margins from the App Store, which already generates Apple an estimated $30 billion a year.

Schiller, now 66 and edging toward retirement, "seems to believe that such moves will only irk developers and governments," he said. Based on what Gurman has heard from internal sources at the company, he added that "there was no internal blowup or anything like that, [but] it's something he wanted no part of."

Schiller said in court that he had concerns that the fee would create an "antagonistic relationship" between Apple and developers, and worried about Apple becoming "some kind of collection agency" that might need to audit developers who didn't pay.

Meanwhile, Apple is now said to be moving responsibility for the ‌App Store‌ to Cue, who oversaw it until 2015, when Schiller took over. Carson Oliver, who has long been on the ‌App Store‌ team, will oversee its day-to-day operations.

App Store Earnings Down

Apple admitted during its July earnings call that regulatory changes have started to weigh on its Services growth. Apple reported services revenue of $30.7 billion for the June quarter, a record for the period but short of the $31.4 billion that analysts expected.

Appfigures said in August that Apple's U.S. commission revenue from the App Store has fallen 18 percent since the start of 2026. It also found App Store revenue declining in Brazil and Japan since both countries introduced new regulations.
