title: Apple Reportedly Planning All-New MacBook Model Between Air and Pro
content:
Apple may introduce an entirely new 13.8-inch OLED MacBook model in 2029, potentially creating a new product tier between the MacBook Air and MacBook Pro, according to an updated product roadmap from research firm Omdia.


The firm's latest roadmap sandwiches a new 13.8-inch MacBook between the projected time line for the Air and Pro models. The surprise model is said to use a single-stack hybrid OLED panel, rather than the more sophisticated tandem OLED technology that is expected in the upcoming OLED MacBook Pro models, which are set to launch either later this year or early next year.

June report from ZDNet Korea, Apple sounded out Samsung Display, LG Display, and BOE for information regarding a 13.8-inch OLED MacBook panel earlier this year. At the time, the general assumption was that it was likely to be part of Apple's work on the first OLED MacBook Air, expected by 2028 at the earliest.

However, looking at Omdia's latest roadmap, the OLED MacBook Air is conspicuously absent, having been replaced by the 13.8-inch OLED machine in a separate "new" product category. The new model is expected to incorporate an LTPO+ backplane, integrated touch sensing, an under-panel camera, and a color filter integrated into the OLED encapsulation layer. 

Omdia believes it is still too early to know for sure which display manufacturer would supply panels for the device, but the firm believes that it could potentially become an important mainstream MacBook product, positioned between the LCD MacBook Air and the higher-end OLED MacBook Pro.

Meanwhile, the MacBook Air line is shown as continuing to use LCD displays right into 2030.


Of course, Apple's wholesale OLED adoption plans could change, and Omdia itself caveats that its roadmap is based on current market expectations. On that basis alone, it could be adjusted at any time according to OLED manufacturing capacity, component costs, and Apple's wider product strategy. Additionally, this is the first we've heard of a completely new MacBook line, and it's still three years out. So with all due caution, file this one under "wait and see."

title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: New features, release date, beta, compatible Macs
content:
Macworld





Apple has already revealed many of the new features coming in macOS 27 Golden Gate, the next major update for the Mac. Headline changes include an all-new Siri AI assistant, major upgrades to apps including Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail and Calendar, expanded child-safety features, design refinements and performance improvements throughout the operating system. We’ve also had the chance to see many of these features in action through the beta, with the full release now likely to be only days away.
Golden Gate continues Apple’s tradition of naming macOS releases after iconic Californian landmarks. More broadly, the update represents another step in Apple’s push to make the Mac smarter and more proactive, with greater use of Apple Intelligence across the operating system and a stronger focus on helping users complete everyday tasks more quickly.
macOS 27 will support all Macs powered by Apple silicon, marking the end of the road for Intel-based Macs. While Intel models won’t be eligible for the new operating system, Apple is expected to continue providing security updates for them for some time.
Apple made developer and public betas of macOS 27 available, with the finished version expected in September 2026. This hub covers everything you need to know about macOS 27 Golden Gate, including its new features, compatibility, beta releases and Apple Intelligence upgrades.


What’s New in macOS 27 Golden Gate at a glance

				
					

				
			
Apple




Here are the top ten new features and changes coming with macOS 27 Golden Gate. 
Siri AI: A redesigned conversational Siri that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access the web and take actions across apps.
Apple Intelligence: Systemwide proofreading, smarter writing tools, improved dictation and automatic file and folder naming.
Safari upgrades: Automatic tab grouping, webpage change alerts with Notify Me, AI-generated extensions and faster, more efficient browsing.
Smarter Messages and Mail: Personalized Smart Reply, better search and syncing, contextual suggestions and improved reliability.
New Photos tools: Spatial Reframing, image expansion with Extend, improved Clean Up and better search and organisation.
More powerful built-in apps: New features for Passwords, Calendar, Notes, Preview, Freeform, Weather, Shortcuts and Image Playground.
Expanded parental controls: Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time, contact approvals and broader Communication Safety protections.
Better Mac gaming: Game Porting Toolkit 4 promises significant performance and compatibility improvements for Windows games.
Refined Liquid Glass design: Better readability and consistency, adjustable transparency, cleaner Finder windows and improved iPhone Mirroring.
Faster macOS performance: Quicker app launches, Spotlight, AirDrop and networking, plus improved external-display, Thunderbolt and Bluetooth support.


						

							


macOS 27 release date: When will macOS 27 be available?
General release TBC, we predict September 14.
In recent years, Apple has released macOS around the same time as iOS, typically on the Monday following its September iPhone launch event. With Apple’s 2026 keynote taking place on Wednesday, September 9, our best guess is that macOS 27 will be released on Monday, September 14.


						

							


macOS 27 Beta – What’s new in the latest beta?
Latest beta: Beta 8, August 31, 2026

				
					

				
			

Apple




Apple released the first macOS 27 developer beta at WWDC, followed by the first public beta on July 13, 2026. The current version is developer beta 8, released on August 31, alongside Public Beta 6.
At this late stage, Apple is mainly refining the software ahead of its expected September release. Recent betas focus on Siri AI, faster performance and search, Safari automation, deeper Apple Intelligence integration and further refinements to Liquid Glass.
Most people should still wait for the final release, particularly if they rely on their Mac for work or use specialist software. Beta software can still cause crashes, app compatibility problems, increased battery drain and, in some cases, data loss. If you do install it, make a full backup first and ideally use a secondary Mac, separate volume or external SSD.
Here’s how you can participate in the beta program we also recommend reading our guide to whether you should install the latest macOS beta.
Separately, the macOS 26.7 release candidate appears to have revealed a substantial part of Apple’s upcoming hardware roadmap, with references to nearly 40 products, including the iPhone Ultra, iPhone 18 range, M6 and OLED MacBook Pros, new iMacs and iPads. Other references point to camera-equipped AirPods, new Home devices, a security camera, tabletop robot, next-generation Vision Pro and further undisclosed products.


						

							


Siri AI: Siri powered macOS 27 features  

				
					

				
			
Foiundry




Apple’s biggest focus in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Siri AI, a completely redesigned version of Siri powered by Apple Intelligence. Rather than functioning primarily as a voice assistant, Siri is becoming a conversational AI that can answer questions, understand personal and onscreen context, access current information from the web and take actions across apps.
We tested Siri AI in beta on a MacBook Neo, and it behaves much more like a generative-AI chatbot than the Siri of old. It can answer questions directly, understand natural follow-ups and solve problems instead of simply directing users to web searches.
At a glance: What’s new with Siri AI?
Conversational AI assistant: Siri can handle open-ended questions, brainstorming, research and natural back-and-forth conversations.
Dedicated Siri app: A standalone Siri app keeps conversations in one place and syncs them through iCloud, allowing users to start a conversation on one Apple device and continue it on another.
Personal context awareness: Siri will be able to understand information in Messages, Mail, Notes, Photos, Maps and files to locate information and provide answers based on your personal data.
Web-powered answers: Siri can access current information from the web, making it more useful for research, learning, interview preparation and questions about recent events.
App actions and automation: Siri can perform tasks across apps such as Messages, Music, Reminders, Calendar and Maps using natural-language instructions.
Spotlight integration: Siri AI is integrated with Spotlight, allowing users to type questions and receive AI-generated answers without opening a browser or separate app.
Visual Intelligence: Visual Intelligence comes to the Mac for the first time, allowing Siri to understand selected images, documents, files, text and other content displayed on screen.

				
					

				
			
Apple’s Visual Intelligence initially placed Blutenburg in Denmark.

Macwelt




Writing Tools: Siri can generate text, rewrite drafts, summarise content and adjust wording or tone. Apple says it can also adapt writing to the way you typically communicate with particular contacts.
Improved dictation: Systemwide dictation gains better speech recognition along with automatic punctuation, capitalisation and formatting.
Custom Siri voices: Users can choose Siri’s voice and adjust characteristics such as pace and expressiveness, although some of these capabilities require newer hardware.
macOS 27 also contains an experimental Siri AI popover seen in the beta. Selecting text can bring up a small Siri icon offering contextual actions including Writing Tools, summaries and key points, sending messages or emails, creating calendar events, opening locations in Maps, and tracking flights or packages. The feature is not currently enabled by default and requires Apple’s FeatureFlags system to activate, suggesting it may still be under development.
Apple also appears to be taking a relatively restrained approach to AI behaviour. In our testing, Siri avoids presenting itself as human, excessive flattery and potentially harmful responses, while generally keeping its answers straightforward.
When will Siri AI be available on Mac? 
Siri AI is already available in beta, and Apple says it will be released to the public “later this year.” We therefore expect it to arrive as an update to macOS 27 and Apple’s other OS 27 releases rather than as part of the initial launch.
Apple has also said Siri AI will still be labelled as a beta when it launches, so users should expect some rough edges and continued improvements after release. 
Siri AI is initially available in English. Availability will vary by region. Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the European Union because of issues related to the Digital Markets Act, and it will remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory approvals. However, it will be available on Mac and Vision Pro in the EU.
Which Macs support Siri AI?
Siri AI requires a Mac that supports Apple Intelligence, but some of its most advanced capabilities have higher hardware requirements.
Apple says its most powerful on-device AI model, expressive Siri voices and advanced dictation require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory. Macs that support Apple Intelligence but do not meet those requirements can still receive other Siri AI features, although the exact feature set may vary.


						

							


Safari features coming in macOS 27

				
					

				
			
Notify Me in Safari

Apple




Safari is getting several Apple Intelligence-powered upgrades in macOS 27, including smarter tab organisation, webpage monitoring, custom extension generation and performance improvements.
Automatic Tab Topics: Safari will automatically group related tabs by topic as you browse, helping keep research and projects organised. These groups can also be saved for later.
Notify Me: Safari will be able to monitor webpages for changes and alert you when something happens, such as a product coming back in stock or a price dropping, removing the need to keep refreshing pages manually.
Describe an Extension: Users will be able to create custom Safari extensions simply by describing what they want. Safari will generate the extension from the text description and add it to the toolbar.
Faster, more efficient browsing: Apple says Safari will use less power while improving page-loading speed, JavaScript performance, scrolling, animations and resizing of the Start Page.

				
					

				
			
Get notified. 

Macwelt



							


Messages and Mail features coming in macOS 27
Messages and Mail are gaining deeper Apple Intelligence integration in macOS 27, alongside improvements to search, syncing and everyday reliability.
Messages
One-Tap Suggestions in Messages: Messages will suggest useful actions based on the context of a conversation, such as creating a reminder or note without leaving the chat.
Smarter Photo Suggestions: Messages will surface relevant photos based on people, places and keywords mentioned in a conversation.
Personalized Smart Reply: Suggested replies can reflect your usual writing style and adapt depending on who you’re messaging.
Improved syncing: Messages should sync more reliably across devices, while failed messages will automatically retry sending.
Mail
Personalized Smart Reply: Mail will also generate suggested responses that better match your writing style and the person you’re replying to.
More relevant search: A new ranking system will prioritise the most useful search results, alongside improved search indexing.
Faster and more accurate: Apple says Mail will load messages more quickly and provide more reliable unread counts.


						

							


Photos features coming in macOS 27
Photos is gaining new AI-powered editing and organisation tools in macOS 27, making it easier to improve images, find photos and manage an iCloud library.
Spatial Reframing: Photos will be able to intelligently recompose and reframe images after they’ve been taken.
Extend Tool: A new Extend tool can expand an image beyond its original boundaries, filling in missing areas when changing the crop or aspect ratio.
Enhanced Clean Up: Apple’s Clean Up tool will be better at removing larger unwanted objects and distractions from photos.
Better organisation and search: Photos adds keywords, star ratings, improved metadata search and other tools for organising a library.
Faster iCloud syncing: iCloud Photos can begin uploads more quickly, with an option to prioritise syncing when needed.


						

							


Other new features coming to apps with macOS 27
macOS 27 also brings a wide range of smaller upgrades across Apple’s built-in apps, with a particular focus on automation, organisation, security and Apple Intelligence.
Passwords
The Passwords app can automatically identify weak or compromised passwords and, with Apple Intelligence, visit supported websites, change the password and save the new credentials. This could remove much of the manual work involved in updating large numbers of old or leaked passwords, although questions remain over website compatibility, two-factor authentication and how consistently the feature will work. Read: Apple finally got rid of my biggest password headache.
Image Playground
Image Playground gets a substantial AI upgrade, including the ability to create photorealistic images and make more convincing edits to existing pictures, such as changing colours, hair and other details. Apple continues to apply safeguards around real people, copyrighted characters and distinctive artistic styles.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Calendar
Calendar gains natural-language event creation, making it possible to describe an event rather than manually entering every detail. It can also make changes to multiple events at once.
Preview
Preview supports more document formats, improves PDF editing and saves PDF files more quickly.
Notes
Notes gains drawing tools for sketching with a mouse or trackpad, along with digital signatures, Markdown copy-and-paste and links to sections within notes.

				
					

				
			
Notes now features a drawing tool as well as the ability to create and use digital signatures.

Foundry




Freeform
Freeform adds drawing tools, collaborative folders and improved organisation, including the ability to sort boards into folders. Full dark-mode support also changes the appearance of the drawing canvas.

				
					

				
			
In Freeform, boards can now be organised into folders.

Foundry




Weather
Weather gets a clearer and more detailed forecast interface, with reorganised information tiles and enhanced 10-day forecasts showing precipitation probability and amount, as well as wind speeds throughout the day.

				
					

				
			
In the Weather app, the tiles have been rearranged, and there are separate 10-day forecasts for precipitation and wind (circled in red).

Foundry




Shortcuts
Shortcuts gains a redesigned editor, more automation capabilities and one of macOS 27’s more ambitious AI features: the ability to turn natural-language instructions into working automations.

				
					

				
			
Shortcuts can start automatically when a specific event occurs.

Thomas Armbrüster




Parental Controls
Apple is expanding its family-safety tools with Safari’s Ask to Browse, improved Screen Time and Time Allowances, contact approvals and broader Communication Safety protections. The changes give parents more control over what children can access and who they can communicate with without completely locking down the Mac.
Accessibility, Shared Albums and Suggestions
macOS 27 also includes accessibility improvements, expanded Shared Albums and more contextual Suggestions throughout the operating system.
Game Porting Toolkit 4
Apple’s Game Porting Toolkit 4 arrives alongside macOS 27 and promises significant improvements for running and porting Windows games on Apple silicon Macs.
Early beta testing suggests substantial performance gains. On an M4 Pro MacBook Pro, GTA V reportedly increased from around 106fps to 176fps, while Red Dead Redemption 2 improved from roughly 60fps to 75fps.
The results suggest software compatibility, rather than raw Apple silicon performance, is increasingly the main obstacle to better Mac gaming. Improvements to Game Porting Toolkit could make Windows titles more practical to run and easier for developers to bring to macOS.


						

							


Design and Interface Changes in macOS 27

				
					

				
			
Apple




macOS 27 Golden Gate refines the Liquid Glass redesign introduced in macOS 26, with Apple focusing on readability, consistency and usability rather than another major visual overhaul.
Changes include:
Improved Liquid Glass: Stronger contrast, better readability and more consistent refraction effects across windows, menus and controls.
Customisable transparency: Users can adjust the Liquid Glass effect in System Settings, from a clearer appearance to a more heavily tinted look.
Cleaner Finder and toolbars: Finder sidebars are more clearly defined, toolbars are more consistent, and edge-to-edge sidebars replace some of the floating elements introduced in macOS 26.
More consistent windows: Window corners, controls and active-window highlighting have been standardised to make the interface feel more coherent.
Updated icons and menus: Menu-bar and app icons gain sharper outlines, improved contrast and more depth, while unnecessary menu icons have been reduced.
Smoother window management: Mission Control and Spaces animations have been refined, and active windows should be easier to distinguish.
New wallpapers and screensavers: Golden Gate-themed backgrounds include animated daytime and nighttime views of the bridge.
Swipe to refresh: Supported Mac apps gain a swipe-down-to-refresh gesture.
Improved iPhone Mirroring: iPhone Mirroring adds Control Center access, resizable app windows and support for DRM-protected video.

				
					

				
			
Foundry



							


Performance improvements and system changes in macOS 27
Apple says macOS 27 focuses on speed, efficiency and everyday usability, with improvements across apps, networking, displays and system tasks. Most of these changes do not require Apple Intelligence.
Changes include:
Faster overall performance: Apps should launch more quickly, while an optimised CPU scheduler improves system responsiveness.
Faster Spotlight and setup: Spotlight indexing and new user-account creation are quicker.
Faster file transfers and networking: AirDrop and network file browsing are faster, while Ethernet status can appear in the menu bar.
Thunderbolt and Bluetooth improvements: RDMA over Thunderbolt has been improved, alongside more efficient Bluetooth power management.
Faster Safari: The Safari Start Page loads more quickly, with broader browser performance improvements.
Better external-display support: New high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes include 5K at 120Hz, alongside improved display-position persistence, HDR support for the macOS interface and 5K Mac mirroring.
Apple Intelligence powered changes:
AI-powered file naming – requires Apple Intelligence: macOS can suggest filenames and folder names based on their contents, including in Pages, Numbers, TextEdit and Finder.
Systemwide proofreading – requires Apple Intelligence: Apple Intelligence provides automatic proofreading and improved spelling and grammar suggestions throughout macOS.
Apple Intelligence privacy: Apple says AI processing happens on-device where possible, with Private Cloud Compute used for more demanding tasks. Data processed in the cloud is not stored or made accessible to Apple.


						

							


macOS 27 Compatible Macs 

				
					

				
			
The MacBook Neo and other Macs in Apple’s current lineup will all be compatible with macOS 27.

Foundry




Apple confirmed that macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with:
MacBook Neo (A18 Pro, 2026)
MacBook Air (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
MacBook Pro (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
iMac (Apple silicon, 2021 and later)
Mac mini (Apple silicon, 2020 and later)
Mac Studio (2022 and later)
Mac Pro (Apple silicon, 2023 and later)
All supported Macs can run Apple Intelligence, although some of the most advanced Siri AI features require an M3 or later Mac with at least 12GB of unified memory.
What about Intel Macs?
macOS 27 marks another major step in Apple’s transition away from Intel. macOS 26 Tahoe was the final version to support Intel Macs, and Apple is now encouraging developers to remove Intel code from their apps and focus on Apple silicon.
macOS 27 will also be the final version to support Rosetta, Apple’s translation technology for running Intel-only apps on Apple silicon Macs. Those apps will continue to work in macOS 27, but will stop working in macOS 28 unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions.
To help users prepare, macOS 27 includes an Intel-app checker in System Settings that lists Intel-based apps used during the past year. If you still rely on any essential Intel-only software, now is a good time to look for updates or alternatives before upgrading to macOS 28.
What happens to DVD support?
macOS 27 also begins the phase-out of Apple’s native DVD support. Apple has removed the DVDPlayback framework from the macOS 27 SDK and says it will disappear completely in a future version of macOS.
Golden Gate may still include the DVD Player app, but it is likely to be the last macOS release with Apple’s built-in DVD playback support. Users who still watch DVDs on a Mac will increasingly need to rely on third-party software such as VLC.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
When will macOS 27 Golden Gate be released?
Apple hasn’t confirmed exactly when macOS 27 will be available to install, but it usually launches to the general public in September, or at the latest October. 
Once macOS 27 launches Apple will likely continue beta development to test new features that weren’t available at launch. 





2.
Should I install the macOS 27 beta?
Whether you should install the macOS 27 beta depends on your needs, technical expertise, and tolerance for bugs and instability. Beta software can introduce crashes, data loss, app compatibility problems, excessive battery drain, reduced performance, and other unexpected issues.
For most users, the recommendation is simple: don’t install it. If you’re eager to try the new features download the Public Beta – but avoid installing it on your primary Mac.
Developers are a different case. The Developer Beta is available now through Apple’s Developer Program, allowing app creators to test their software against new APIs, frameworks, and system features before the public release. If you’re not a developer, think carefully before installing the Developer Beta, as it is typically less stable and more prone to bugs than later beta releases.
Regardless of which beta you choose, make sure you have a complete backup of your Mac before upgrading.





3.
Which Macs can run macOS 27?
All M-series Macs will get macOS 27, and the MacBook Neo. 
Certain Siri AI features – most powerful on-device model, expressive voices and advanced dictation – will only be available for M3 Macs and newer.





4.
Should Intel Mac owners upgrade now?
Intel Mac owners should upgrade to Apple Silicon as soon as possible. The transition away from Intel hardware has reached a critical turning point, with software support rapidly vanishing and a new generation of affordable entry-level hardware making the switch more accessible than ever.
Apple has confirmed that macOS 27 will not support any Intel-based Macs. While a small number of Intel models may receive security patches for older versions of macOS until September 2028, they are already excluded from modern flagship features.
Those with Intel Macs also miss out on many features, including Apple Intelligence.





5.
Will macOS 27 support Rosetta and Intel apps?
macOS 27 will still run Intel-only Mac apps through Rosetta 2. However, macOS 27 will be the final version of macOS to support Rosetta 2 as a general-purpose translation technology for running Intel-based Mac apps on Apple silicon.
Rosetta has acted as a transition layer since Apple introduced its own Mac chips in 2020, translating x86_64 Intel instructions so older software can run on Apple silicon. After macOS 27, most Intel-only Mac apps will no longer work unless developers release Apple silicon-native versions, although Apple will retain limited Rosetta functionality for some older, unmaintained games.
Apple is already preparing users for the change. Since macOS 26.4, Macs can display warnings when launching apps that rely on Rosetta, encouraging users to update to Apple silicon-native versions before general Rosetta support ends.
In macOS 28, most Intel-only apps will no longer run unless developers update them for Apple silicon.





6.
When is macOS usually updated?
Here is a history of release dates for macOS:
macOS 26 Tahoe: September 15, 2025
macOS 15 Sequoia: September 16, 2024
macOS 14 Sonoma: September 26, 2023
macOS 13 Ventura: October 25, 2022
macOS 12 Monterey: October 25, 2021
macOS 11 Big Sur: November 19, 2020
macOS 10.15 Catalina: October 7, 2019
macOS 10.14 Mojave: September 24, 2018
macOS 10.13 High Sierra: September 25, 2017
macOS 10.12 Sierra: September 20, 2016

title: iPhone 18 Pro Chip Leak Indicates Major GPU and Memory Bandwidth Improvements
content:
An alleged solder joint diagram for Apple's A20 Pro chip suggests the processor will deliver a number of significant upgrades, including a seven-core GPU, a wider memory interface, and a larger L2 cache for its efficiency cores.


The claims come from a Weibo user who says the layout was reconstructed by mapping the chip's solder ball positions and overlaying them with die level images to sketch out where each block of the processor sits. According to the post, the resulting outline points to a two and four core CPU configuration and a seven core GPU, with the top of the die housing the GPU and the CPU occupying the center.

Based on the layout, the leaker expects the A20 Pro's efficiency cores to share an 8MB L2 cache, up from 6MB on the A19 Pro, while the performance cores retain their existing 16MB L2 cache. The size of the shared system level cache is not yet known, but the leaker believes it is unlikely to shrink given the chip's new image signal processor and neural engine.

With regards to the GPU, the seven core configuration would mark an increase from the six cores on the A19 Pro, a jump of roughly 16%. The leak also points to a 96-bit memory interface for LPDDR5x RAM, up from the 64-bit interface on the A19 Pro, a 50% increase that would meaningfully boost memory bandwidth. Graphics performance tends to scale with memory bandwidth, so the wider bus could have an additional impact on top of the additional GPU core.

iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max next week. It could also be used in Apple's first foldable iPhone.

title: iPhone 18 Pro leak claims the A20 Pro will have dramatic GPU gains
content:
Macworld





A leak on the Chinese social media site Weibo, 白饭炒白米饭, has posted images of what are purported to be the solder joint diagram for the A20 Pro (the diagram showing all the little contact points by which the chip is attached to the board beneath). This account has correctly leaked details of some Apple chips or products in the past.
From there, the leaker has used the layout and the previous chip block diagram to estimate some of the layout of the new A20 chip—a rough diagram of some of the major components.

				
					

				
			Weibo – 白饭炒白米饭
There are three details gleaned from this process, if you trust in its accuracy.
First, we have seven GPU cores. The A19 Pro has six.
Second, there’s a 96-bit memory interface for LPDD5x RAM. The A19 Pro had a 64-bit interface.
Third, there will still be a 6-core CPU configuration, with two high-performance cores and four efficiency cores.
How does all this compare to the A19 Pro, and what could it mean? Well, the smaller efficiency cores all share a single 8MB L2 cache, which is 2MB more than before. That will speed things up a bit when the efficiency cores do bigger jobs on larger data sets. The two performance cores share a 16MB L2 cache (two 8MB blocks in the diagram), which is the same as before.
It’s not clear if any of these cores have architectural design changes or if these cores are Apple’s “Super Cores.”
Going up from 6 GPU cores to 7 is an increase of about 16 percent. We think it’s likely that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will have all GPU cores enabled, but the folding iPhone Ultra (very thin and difficult to cool) will have one core disabled, just as the iPhone Air has one A19 Pro GPU core disabled.
Graphics performance tends to be highly constrained by memory bandwidth, which is where the change to the memory interface gets interesting. Apple is not making the jump to LPDDR6 this year, sticking with LPDDR5x again, but a 50 percent wider interface means 50 percent more memory bandwidth. If Apple increases the memory clock speed, it can be even more.
So while there are “only” 16 percent more GPU cores, the increase in memory bandwidth and the potential for higher clock speeds or GPU core architectural improvements means that we can expect 20-30 percent higher GPU performance. That’s not unprecedented, but it’s more than we predicted in our A20 preview.
AI is increasingly important to Apple, and it shares many core architectural features between its A-series mobile chips and its M-series chips for Macs. So it makes sense that Apple is investing heavily in GPU performance, memory bandwidth, and GPU compute features—all of which help with running or training local AI models. Fortunately, even if you don’t care about AI performance, all of this increased GPU performance and memory bandwidth will also mean better performance for 3D games and other graphics-intensive apps and tasks.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Prices Estimated Ahead of Apple Event Next Week
content:
Less than a week before Apple debuts new iPhone 18 Pro models, research firm TrendForce has estimated the prices of the devices based on the latest hardware cost environment.


TrendForce's price estimates compared to last year's models look like this:

  

    Model

June forecast of a 14-18% increase, which fits within its latest broader 10-20% range and translates more neatly to Apple's typical pricing scheme, we could see the iPhone 18 Pro starting price jump to between $1,249-$1,299 and the iPhone 18 Pro Max between $1,349-$1,399.

Meanwhile, TrendForce expects prices for Apple's first foldable iPhone (aka "iPhone Ultra") to start anywhere between $2,099-$2,299, with the highest storage option potentially exceeding $3,000.

The regular iPhone 18 model is not expected to debut until spring 2027. Nevertheless, TrendForce expects the same general 10-20% price increase to apply to that device as well.

The overriding reason for the price increases is memory costs. TrendForce says the cost of a 256GB memory chip has risen nearly 400% year-on-year, while its separate analysis puts the overall bill of materials (BOM) for a 256GB Pro model at around 38% more over the same period. That said, Apple is expected to absorb some of that increase via lower margins, rather than passing the full cost onto consumers.

Last year, Apple managed to avoid raising the price of the iPhone 17 Pro Max, and only marginally raised the iPhone 17 Pro price in the U.S. year-on-year by $100. This year, however, the insatiable AI infrastructure buildout has made memory costs even more expensive, effectively holding the rest of the electronics industry to ransom. And things don't look like they're going to get any better anytime soon.

title: Why Apple’s folding iPhone will be ‘Ultra’ in name only
content:
Macworld





Apple is preparing to expand its Ultra line in a big way. The designation, currently limited to Apple Watches, M-series chips, and CarPlay, will reportedly come to the iPhone next, with the launch of the first folding iPhone on September 9. Per Apple’s nomenclature, an Ultra product is the highest-end of its kind, outperforming the Pro models with high-end features worthy of its name and price. That, however, won’t be the case when the iPhone Ultra launches in a few weeks.
The iPhone Ultra will undoubtedly cost the most and offer exclusive features unavailable on Pro iPhones, most notably a folding display and upgraded iOS multitasking. Nevertheless, it’ll miss out on a ton of essential features that users already get with Pro phones and, in some cases, even entry-level iPhones. When evaluating the full packages, one could arguably crown the iPhone 18 Pro Max as this year’s actual Ultra model.
Faceless ID
Users will experience the downgrade from the moment they pick up their iPhone Ultra. Due to its complex folding design, Face ID, the decade-old biometric authenticator and standard across all iPhone models, will reportedly be missing from a flagship iPhone for the first time since 2017. Instead, you’ll have to precisely position your registered finger on the Touch ID sensor embedded into the power button, as wth the iPad.
I’ve used Apple’s side-mounted Touch ID reader on an iPad Air in the past, and, trust me, you wouldn’t want it on your primary device. The operating system relies on biometric authentication for numerous sensitive tasks, beyond merely unlocking your iDevice. It’s used for Apple Pay, Apple Passwords, App Store purchases, etc. If your fingertip is moist or you’re wearing gloves, you’re going to find yourself manually entering your iPhone’s passcode countless times per day.

				
					

				
			
The iPhone Ultra will reportedly have just two cameras, a stark downgrade from the Pro phones.

Foundry




Camera shy
iPhones are many users’ sole digital cameras, with the Pro models boasting three advanced rear lenses for wide, ultra-wide, and telephoto shots. Given the Ultra name’s perceived superiority, customers would assume that the folding iPhone would match or even outdo the Pro variants in photography. In reality, it likely won’t.
According to rumors, the iPhone Ultra will completely drop the telephoto lens, downgrading the maximum digital zoom from 40x to around 10x. This will bar users from taking crisp shots of faraway subjects. Furthermore, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is rumored to exclusively adopt a variable aperture main camera, letting you control the depth of field and produce more balanced photos. You won’t get that with an iPhone Ultra, either.
Lack of Action
A couple of years ago, the iPhone 15 Pro retired the classic mute switch in favor of an all-new Action button. The mappable button allows users to run any task by pressing and holding it, including custom shortcuts, menus, and conditionals, making the Action button highly personalizable and useful. Based on the latest reports, the iPhone Ultra will exclude the Action button, providing users without an easy way to perform frequent daily actions.
Another common iPhone feature that might be missing is MagSafe. Not only does MagSafe provide a more reliable wireless charging experience and unlock StandBy mode, but it also lets you effortlessly attach a wide range of accessories, including wallets, power banks, kickstands, tripods, and much, much more. 
While the necessary magnets are incorporated into all iPhone models—including the $599 17e—the $2,000-2,500 iPhone Ultra might skip it, according to some rumors. However, a report just this week claims that Apple’s folding phone will indeed have MagSafe, so if you’re hoping to buy one, keep your fingers crossed.

				
					

				
			
The Action button has become a standard feature on all flagship iPhones—but it might not be coming to the Ultra.

Foundry




Handle with care
With the highest water and dust resistance, we no longer think twice before rinsing our iPhones or bringing them to the beach. The iPhone 17 Pro, for example, has the highest ingress protection rating: 68. The 6 refers to its dust-tight seal that prevents fine particles from entering the device, while the 8 indicates you can immerse it in up to 1.5 meters of water for no more than 30 minutes.
Foldable phones typically come with a lower IP rating due to their more complex design, including the mechanical hinge. Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8—which reportedly mimics the iPhone Ultra form factor—has an IP48 rating. So, while it’s generally resistant to water, the 4 translates to vulnerability towards particles finer than 1mm. Beach sand, pocket lint, and dirt can get inside the phone and potentially damage it down the road, so you’ll need to be a lot more careful when carrying it around.
Simple SIM
Lastly, the iPhone Ultra, like the iPhone Air, will reportedly be eSIM-only internationally. While all iPhones sold in the US migrated to this format long ago, many frequent fliers and international users still prefer physical SIMs for a number of reasons. title: Anker's New MindBase Home Hub Runs AI Locally, Doubles as NAS
content:
Anker today announced the launch of Anker MindBase, an AI home hub meant to work with almost 100 Anker devices and Matter-enabled smart home devices from other companies. It works alongside HomeKit, and is equipped with an AI Core compute card and the on-device Anker TrueSmart AI Agent.


In addition to working as a smart home hub, the MindBase supports up to 48TB of local storage, and it functions as a NAS. It can be used for storing files, photos, and videos locally. MindBase integrates with Anker security cameras, and Anker plans to sell a MindBase Security Kit that includes a new TrackLight Cam S1, S4 Video Doorbell, and Smart Security Shield sensor.

Anker says on-device AI evaluates events in real time to assess risk and respond through observation, lighting, verbal warnings, or active deterrence. The sensor can be placed at the edge of a property, using radar to detect strangers from up to 15 meters away.


Anker is also debuting several new home security products.

 	
Eufy Video Doorbell S4 - The Video Doorbell S4 is a wired doorbell and security camera combo. It has a 9-megapixel lens with 3K resolution and a 180-degree field of view.

Eufy Fall Detection Sensor - The Fall Detection Sensor is a non-wearable sensor that uses mmWave radar sensing to detect falls without using a camera. It can be mounted on the wall and supports two-way communication.

 	
Eufy NVR Security System E50 - The E50 pairs an 8-channel network video recorder with four hybrid bullet pan-tilt-zoom dual-lens camera. There's a 2K resolution wide-angle bullet lens and a motorized 4K resolution PTZ lens.


Eufy website starting at $999. The Video Doorbell S4 is priced at $300 and will be available in late September. The Window Camera E10 will be available later this year for $70. Availability and pricing have not yet been announced for the MindBase and Fall Detection Sensor.

title: Foldable 'iPhone Ultra' Still Likely to Be Missing These Five Features
content:
Apple's first foldable iPhone, dubbed the "iPhone Ultra," is expected to launch without at least four features that will be present on the iPhone 18 Pro models, despite a price tag of at least $2,000.



iPhone Air lacks Ultra Wide and Telephoto rear cameras, a SIM card slot, and stereo speakers. With a super thin design, a titanium frame, and a glass back, the ‌iPhone Ultra‌ is expected to be very similar to the ‌iPhone Air‌ in terms of design, and it is possible that similar concessions will be present on the device. There are no indications that the ‌iPhone Ultra‌ will be missing stereo speakers, but it is not out of the question given the other compromises Apple has chosen to make. Based on over a year of reports and rumors, the ‌iPhone Ultra‌ could be missing the following features:


	
Face ID/TrueDepth camera array

	
Telephoto camera/third rear camera

	
Action button

	
Physical SIM card slot

	
mmWave 5G


MagSafe was originally in question earlier in the rumor cycle. 


Face ID

The ‌iPhone Ultra‌ is believed to be too thin to accommodate Apple's TrueDepth camera array, which is required for ‌Face ID‌ authentication, so Apple is expected to revert to a Touch ID side button instead.

front-facing camera for both displays, with the inner one rumored to be a 24-megapixel under-display sensor, but biometric authentication will be handled by the fingerprint reader.

Touch ID was 2016's iPhone 7. The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models are moving in the opposite direction, apparently relocating ‌Face ID‌'s flood illuminator beneath the screen to shrink the Dynamic Island.

Telephoto Camera

As visible on dummy models shared by Sonny Dickson, Vadim Yuryev, and others, the ‌iPhone Ultra‌ is expected to sport only two rear cameras. These are believed to be 48-megapixel Wide and Ultra Wide lenses, with no third Telephoto camera of the kind found on the Pro models. 

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said last month that the people who have used the device are impressed by it, but singled out the camera system as the most likely disappointment for buyers.

Action Button

Dummy models continue to point to the absence of the Action button. A power button and volume buttons are clearly visible, with the volume buttons located on the top edge of the device and aligned to the right, similar to the iPad mini, but the left edge appears to be entirely bare. That would make the ‌iPhone Ultra‌ the first iPhone with no Action button or silent switch, some three years after Apple introduced the Action button on the iPhone 15 Pro as a replacement for the switch.

Instant Digital," who said that the motherboard sits on the right side of the device. Rather than run cables across the display to the left side, where the volume buttons are located on every other iPhone, Apple is said to have decided to run them directly upwards to maximize internal space.

Image via Vadim Yuryev.


SIM Card Slot

Rumors indicate that the ‌iPhone Ultra‌ will also lack a SIM card slot, just like the ‌iPhone Air‌, being compatible with eSIM only. Gurman and analyst Ming-Chi Kuo both expect the device to be eSIM only in every market where it launches.

mmWave 5G Connectivity

The device is likely to miss mmWave 5G if it features Apple's in-house C2 modem as rumored, since reports indicate the C2 may still lack mmWave capability. ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models sold in the United States are expected to retain Qualcomm hardware because they support the mmWave bands used by American carriers. Apple does not sell mmWave-capable iPhones outside the U.S.

The ‌iPhone Ultra‌'s C2-based configuration would therefore advance Apple's modem transition, just like the ‌iPhone Air‌, but could limit the device to sub-6GHz 5G.

MagSafe?

Bloomberg's ‌Mark Gurman‌ has now indicated that ‌MagSafe‌ will make it into the device after all. Speaking in an interview with Tom's Guide, Gurman said "all indications that I've heard is that ‌MagSafe‌ is in for this foldable phone," pointing to the fact that Apple managed to fit the magnet array into the ‌iPhone Air‌.

The uncertainty stemmed from the dummy models of the device that emerged earlier this year. Units shared by Dickson and Yuryev showed no indentations for the internal ‌MagSafe‌ magnets, while the mock ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max units shown alongside them clearly did. Leaked cases for the foldable, on the other hand, included a magnetic ring, leaving the question open until recently.

Image via Vadim Yuryev.


Price and Launch

The rumored starting price for the ‌iPhone Ultra‌ varies, but reports agree that it will not be below $1,999, with Kuo placing it somewhere between $2,000 and $2,500. The iPhone 17 Pro starts at $1,099 and has all of the above features, and while the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ is expected to see a price increase of $200 to $300, the ‌iPhone Ultra‌'s compromises could still prove controversial.

title: iOS 27 Introduces New 'iPhone Handoff' Feature
content:
Apple has added a new "iPhone Handoff" feature to iOS 27 that will allow you to switch between two iPhones while using the same phone number on each device.


This functionality was briefly mentioned during the WWDC 2026 keynote in June, on a slide that listed hundreds of new features coming in iOS 27 and corresponding software updates, but Apple never shared any further details at the time.

MacRumors forum member pdfu today shared a video that demonstrates how the feature will work, using two simulated iPhones running in Xcode 27's Device Hub.

"iPhone Handoff" can be set up from the Settings app, under the Cellular menu. During the setup process, you can choose which iPhone you want to be the main device that you use most often and which one you want to be the companion device.

Apple says a user's main eSIM will remain on the main iPhone, while the companion iPhone will receive a companion eSIM, and this will enable you to switch between the devices back and forth while using the same phone number.

All cellular settings are managed on the main iPhone, and location sharing is based on whichever iPhone is actively using the phone number.

In addition to needing two iPhones running iOS 27, "iPhone Handoff" will seemingly require carrier support. The forum post mentions that T-Mobile in the U.S. and Deutsche Telekom in Germany might be among the first carriers to offer the feature.

title: iOS 27: Release date, Beta, compatible iPhones and all new features
content:
Macworld





Apple has already previewed the new features coming to compatible iPhones with iOS 27, including major Apple Intelligence upgrades, changes to Siri, stronger parental controls and improvements across core iPhone apps. We’ve also had the chance to see many of these features in action through the beta, and the full release is now only days away.
iOS 27 is currently available as a beta for developers and public testers after several months of testing. Apple typically releases major iOS updates in September, often around the second week, making Monday, September 14 a likely release date based on previous years.
iOS 27 will support every iPhone back to the iPhone 11 and iPhone SE (2nd generation), although some Apple Intelligence and Siri features will require newer hardware.
This hub covers everything Apple has confirmed for iOS 27, including new features, compatible iPhones, beta updates, Apple Intelligence improvements and what’s changing with Siri. We also cover notable discoveries from the beta and the latest rumors ahead of launch.


What’s New in iOS 27 at a Glance
Siri AI: Apple’s new Siri AI combines personal context, onscreen awareness and web knowledge to deliver more natural conversations, richer answers, app actions and cross-device chat history.
Apple Intelligence across apps: Apple Intelligence expands across Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail, Calendar, Home and Shortcuts, adding smarter suggestions, automation, image generation and context-aware assistance.
Smarter Photos editing: Photos gains Spatial Reframing, Extend and an upgraded Clean Up tool, allowing users to improve composition, expand images and remove distractions more naturally.
Child safety and parental controls: New parental controls include Ask to Browse, Time Allowances, app schedules and enhanced Communication Safety tools designed to give parents more control.
Safari and productivity upgrades: Safari can organise tabs, monitor webpages and build extensions from descriptions, while Passwords, Calendar and Shortcuts gain powerful new AI-powered capabilities.


						

							


iOS 27 release date: When will Apple release iOS 27?
September 2026
iOS 27 has been in beta since it was unveiled at WWDC in June, but the official version of iOS 27 will not be available to install on compatible iPhones until later in 2026. 
Apple has confirmed that the iPhone launch event will take place on September 9, so we anticipate that iOS 27 will be available to download on Monday, September 14, as the iOS download usually closely follows Apple’s September event. 


						

							


What is the latest iOS 27 beta?
As of August 31, iOS 27 beta 8 is now available to developers, with the public beta expected shortly.
At this late stage in the development cycle, Apple is focusing on stability rather than adding new features, with recent betas mainly delivering bug fixes, security updates, performance improvements and final polish ahead of launch.


						

							


Siri AI in iOS 27 

				
					

				
			
Apple




By far the biggest upgrade coming in iOS 27 is Siri AI – Apple’s new Apple Intelligence-powered version of Siri. Apple says it is more personal, conversational and capable than the current assistant, with support for natural follow-up questions, personal context, onscreen awareness and up-to-date information from the web.
Siri AI features
More natural conversations: Siri AI can understand open-ended questions, follow-up requests and more complex natural language, making interactions feel less like issuing simple voice commands.
Personal context: Siri can draw on information stored in Messages, Mail, Photos and Notes to find details and answer questions. For example, you could ask it to find information buried in an old email or message.
Onscreen awareness: Siri can understand what you’re viewing and act on it, such as saving an address from a message, adding an event to Calendar or answering questions about an article.
Camera intelligence: A new Siri Camera mode lets you show Siri something through the iPhone’s camera, then ask questions or perform actions based on what it sees.
More capable app actions: Siri can perform tasks within apps such as Messages, Music and Reminders. It can, for example, edit a recently sent message, add a song to a playlist or handle more complex Apple Music requests.
Better general knowledge and web answers: Siri can use information from the web to answer questions about recent events and tackle more specific or complicated queries than before.
Conversation history across devices: A dedicated Siri app lets users revisit previous conversations, pin important chats and continue conversations across Apple devices using iCloud syncing.
More natural Siri voices: Siri gains more expressive voices, with controls on compatible devices for adjusting speaking pace and expressiveness. Voice customisation requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air or newer.
Improved dictation: Better speech recognition, automatic punctuation, capitalisation and formatting allow users to dictate more naturally when converting speech into text.
AI-assisted message replies: Siri can compose contextual replies in Messages using the conversation, personal information and web searches. Shortcuts can also automate replies to selected contacts, although manual Siri-assisted replies allow users to check and edit the response before it is sent.
For more Siri AI message replies read about what happened when we made Siri AI Answer all our Messages. 
How good is Siri AI?
Siri AI represents a significant improvement over the old Siri, particularly when handling conversational questions, current information and personal context.
Early testing suggests it can deal with far more complicated requests than Siri previously could. Apple Music is a good example: Siri can identify very specific groups of songs, create playlists and combine music knowledge with reasoning.
It could therefore become one of the biggest reasons to upgrade to iOS 27, potentially changing Siri from a basic voice-command system into a more general way of interacting with the iPhone.
However, Siri AI is still in beta. Testing has revealed server failures, incorrect answers, weak reasoning and unexplained limitations, so its usefulness will depend heavily on how much Apple improves reliability before release.
Apple’s approach to AI safety also appears more restrained than some rival chatbots, with Siri designed to avoid excessive flattery, pretending to be human or responding inappropriately to potentially harmful requests.
When will Siri AI launch?
Apple says iOS 27 arrives in autumn 2026, but Siri AI does not yet have a specific public release date. Apple currently says a Siri AI beta will be available in English later in 2026.
Regional Siri AI availability
Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the EU. It will also remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory issues.
Siri AI compatibility
Some Siri AI features have more demanding hardware requirements than others. In particular, Apple’s new Siri voice customisation controls require an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air or newer.


						

							


Apple Intelligence across apps
As well as Siri AI, the enhanced Apple Intelligence will also power new AI-powered features in Apple’s core apps throughout iOS 27. Safari will organise tabs into topics, monitor webpages for changes and even build extensions from natural-language descriptions. Photos is set to gain a new Spatial Reframing edit tools including an upgraded Clean Up feature. Messages, Mail and Calendar will be able to understand context, suggest actions and create events from simple descriptions.


						

							


New features coming to apps in iOS 27
iOS 27 brings a mix of major Apple Intelligence upgrades and smaller quality-of-life improvements across Safari, Photos, Messages, AirPods, Passwords, Wallet and other core iPhone apps. Apple is also making iOS more adaptable to different screen sizes and orientations, changes that appear to be laying some of the groundwork for its expected folding iPhone.
Safari
Safari will automatically group tabs into topics, making related pages easier to find. A new Notify Me feature will monitor webpages and alert you to changes such as price drops or products coming back into stock.
Apple is also adding Describe an Extension, which lets users create custom Safari extensions simply by explaining what they want the extension to do.

				
					

				
			

Apple




Photos
Photos gains significantly more powerful AI editing tools.
Spatial Reframing/Reframe can alter the composition and perspective of an existing photo, while Extend generates new image content beyond the original frame when straightening a horizon or changing the aspect ratio.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Clean Up has also been improved, with Fast and High Quality modes for removing unwanted objects. High Quality mode can produce considerably more natural results, although more ambitious edits can still introduce distortions or invented details.
Photos also adds new categories and the ability to save a frame from a video as a full-resolution photo. The resulting HEIF or JPG retains the video’s original resolution, date and location metadata rather than simply creating a screenshot.
Camera
Apple is developing a customizable Camera interface, although it has not appeared consistently throughout the iOS 27 beta cycle. It could arrive in a later iOS 27 update.
Apple is also reportedly developing Apple Reference Image, an authentication system designed to prove that a photo or video was genuinely captured on an iPhone and has not subsequently been manipulated.
The feature would use additional metadata and Apple’s Private Cloud Compute to authenticate an image and assign it a unique ID. Its usefulness may be greatest for journalists, insurers and investigators rather than as a general solution to AI-generated imagery, particularly because authentication would be optional and social networks frequently remove metadata.
Messages

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Messages gets several useful improvements.
You can also decide what the microphone button beside the text field does. Under Settings > Apps > Messages > Show in Text Field, it can be set to Record Audio, Start Dictation or None. Disabling it does not remove either feature: dictation remains available from the keyboard and audio messages remain in the + menu.
Voice-message playback controls are easier to access, while Apple Intelligence can suggest actions based on a conversation, such as creating a reminder, making a note or finding relevant photos.
Messages will also gain smarter suggested replies that can better reflect the user’s writing style.
Drawing

				
					

				
			
Foundry




A new dedicated Drawing app replaces the old hidden handwriting interface. Accessible from the + menu, it uses the familiar pens, colours and drawing controls found in Notes and Markup, with finished drawings sent as images.
Mail
Mail gains more context-aware smart replies, including responses that can better match the user’s usual writing style.
Apple Intelligence can also surface information from Mail elsewhere in iOS. For example, the Phone app could retrieve a flight confirmation number from an email when you call an airline.
Phone
A new Call Context feature can surface information that may be useful when calling a business. Apple says the information is selected according to who you are calling rather than by listening to the conversation. For example, calling an airline could cause iOS to surface the relevant flight confirmation from Mail.
Birthday reminders can also appear when calling contacts whose birthdays are stored on the iPhone.
FaceTime
FaceTime gains Dual Capture, allowing the front and rear cameras to be used at the same time during a call.
Passwords

				
					

				
			
Passwords in iOS 27 will fix things for you.

Apple




The Passwords app will continue to warn about weak, reused and compromised credentials, but iOS 27 goes a step further by offering to fix some of them automatically.
Using Apple Intelligence, Passwords can visit supported websites, change a vulnerable password and save the replacement credentials. See: Apple got rid of my biggest password headache.
The usefulness of the feature will depend on how widely websites are supported and how well it handles obstacles such as two-factor authentication and unusual account-management interfaces.
Shortcuts
Shortcuts gains Describe a Shortcut, allowing users to create automations simply by explaining what they want to happen.
Apple Intelligence will interpret the request and assemble the appropriate actions across supported apps, potentially making Shortcuts significantly easier to use for people unfamiliar with building automations manually.
Calendar
Calendar can create or modify events from natural-language instructions.
Apple says the app can recognise contacts, locations, dates and other event details as users type, reducing the amount of information that needs to be entered manually.
Image Playground
Image Playground is becoming considerably more powerful.
Apple says it can create photorealistic images and lets users modify generated pictures simply by describing the changes they want. Individual objects can also be selected, resized or repositioned.
AI-generated images will include a SynthID watermark identifying them as synthetic content.
Wallet
Wallet can create custom passes from QR codes.
Users can add their own fields and information to the pass, and passes automatically sync to Apple Watch.
Weather
Weather gets a clearer, more detailed forecast interface, with rearranged information tiles and new 10-day views showing precipitation probability/amount and wind speed throughout each day.
Home app
Apple Intelligence comes to the Home app for compatible HomeKit Secure Video cameras. It can group related camera notifications, describe recorded video and highlight clips that appear particularly noteworthy.
Maps
Apple Maps improves Flyover using higher-quality aerial imagery and Visual Intelligence models.
Apple says this produces sharper architectural detail and more realistic rendering of elements such as individual trees.
Podcasts
Video podcasts become easier to use, with improved controls for switching between watching a podcast and simply listening to it.
Fitness
Workout summaries have been redesigned to make them easier to share.
Users can also hide completed Fitness+ workouts.


						

							


iOS 27 changes beyond the iPhone 
CarPlay
CarPlay gains an audio scrubber, giving drivers and passengers more direct control when moving through audio tracks and other content.
AirPods
iOS 27 introduces several new AirPods features.
A new Custom EQ lets users independently adjust bass, mids and treble using a simple three-band equalizer under Settings > AirPods > Audio and Routing > Equalizer > Custom.
Compatible AirPods also gain improved Precision Finding through Find My, making individual earbuds easier to locate.
Some features require both iOS 27 and compatible AirPods firmware.
Read How to tune your AirPods with a custom EQ in iOS 27.


						

							


Other changes coming with iOS 27
It’s not only individual apps that will see changes. 
Home Screen and landscape mode
Apple is making iOS significantly more flexible when dealing with different screen orientations and sizes.
More Apple apps now work properly in landscape, including Health, Home, Music, Weather and Watch. Dynamic Island and Live Activities can also adapt to landscape orientation. The Home Screen additionally supports extra-large widgets.
These changes could simply improve iPhone usability, but they also appear well suited to Apple’s expected folding iPhone, which is likely to have an unusual, wider aspect ratio.
Evidence within Apple’s software also includes new foldState and angleDegrees variables that could allow apps to respond to whether a device is folded and at what angle.
iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 has similarly become freely resizable, with Apple apps dynamically rearranging their interfaces as the window changes shape.
Liquid Glass refinements

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple says Liquid Glass has been refined for better readability, more uniform refraction and improved contrast. A new slider lets users adjust the look from ultraclear to fully tinted, while updated icons, toolbars, sidebars and window shapes add polish.
Ringtones, alarms and alert volume
iOS 27 finally separates several sound-volume controls.
Instead of one combined Ringtone and Alerts slider, users can independently adjust:
Ringtones
Alarms and timers
Alerts and system sounds
The change is optional. Under Settings > Sounds & Haptics, turning off Match Ringtone Volume reveals separate controls.
Media and call volume continue to work independently as before.
Keyboard
iOS 27 introduces a new quick-paste control above the keyboard.
It lets you paste recently copied text, images or screenshots without having to long-press inside a text field, making everyday copy-and-paste considerably faster.
Apple has also made the Liquid Glass keyboard design more consistent across apps.
Privacy and Find My
iOS 27 introduces the ability to temporarily pause Find My location sharing without notifying the person with whom the location is normally shared.
Recovery and troubleshooting
Apple is also expanding the iPhone’s recovery interface, giving users more options for diagnosing problems and recovering an iPhone without immediately connecting it to another device.


						

							


System changes and how iOS 27 will make your iPhone faster
Alongside the headline AI features, Apple says iOS 27 includes a wide range of under-the-hood improvements designed to make iPhones faster, smoother and more efficient.
Apple says apps can launch up to 30% faster, newly taken photos can appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster, and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% quicker. External drive transfers should also improve, while updates to network performance and the system-wide search index are designed to make connectivity and finding information faster.
The company has also reworked core technologies including CPU scheduling, display performance and processing efficiency. These changes should benefit older iPhones in particular, with Apple promising smoother performance and more efficient battery use on devices as old as the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE.
Our testing of the iOS 27 beta supports those claims. On an iPhone 11 Pro Max, Camera launch time fell from 0.98 seconds in iOS 26 to 0.65 seconds in iOS 27, while Maps improved from 3.01 seconds to 1.36 seconds.
Everyday use also feels smoother, with more fluid animations, unlocking, Control Center and app transitions. The phone ran cooler during testing too, which could point to improved system efficiency and potentially better battery performance.
More broadly, iOS 27 appears focused on refinement rather than simply adding new features. Apple says it has addressed dozens of common user frustrations, while changes such as more adjustable Liquid Glass effects are intended to improve readability and general usability.
That focus should make iOS 27 particularly worthwhile for owners of older iPhones, even on models that do not support Siri AI. Those devices still gain performance improvements alongside features such as clipboard tools for the keyboard, independent alarm and timer volume controls, custom Wallet passes, Photos changes, larger widgets and Liquid Glass refinements.


						

							


Child safety and parental controls

				
					

				
			
Apple




There are lots of improvements coming to parental controls, including new time allowances for entertainment, games, and social media, and new schedule tools for different times of day or days of the week.
This includes new features like an expansion of the existing “ask to buy” feature for apps to websites. Before a child can view a new website, they’ll have to ask for permission.
Ask to Browse: Ask to Browse will expand the current Ask to Buy feature to the web. Apple says children will need to request permission before visiting new websites, and parents can review requests in Messages before approving.
Communication Safety: Communication Safety will continue to help protect children from viewing or sharing nudity in Messages, FaceTime and other apps. Apple says it will also intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos.
Time Allowances and schedules: Parents will be able to set Time Allowances across categories such as Entertainment, Games and Social Media. Recommendations are based on a child’s age combined with guidance from clinical and child development experts. Schedules let parents choose which apps are available at different times or on different days.
Redesigned Screen Time: Screen Time will get a redesigned interface with an at-a-glance view of average device usage and most-used apps. Apple says parents can quickly limit or extend access in the moment.
Child accounts and family safety: Apple says child accounts remain central to age-appropriate protections. Parents can manage app access, web access, communication permissions and Screen Time settings. 
Apple says it is working with the American Academy of Pediatrics to adapt its Family Media Plan. 


						

							


Accessibility changes coming in iOS 27 
Accessibility features will be smarter and more intuitive in iOS 27:
VoiceOver will get richer image descriptions and better understanding of onscreen content. 
Live Recognition will let users press the Action button to ask questions about their surroundings and receive detailed responses.
Voice Control will become more intuitive, allowing users to describe onscreen buttons and controls rather than remembering exact labels or numbers. 
Accessibility Reader will be able to handle more complex source material and provide summaries and translation.


						

							


iOS 27 compatibility 

				
					

				
			iPhone 11 is supported by iOS 27.
Roman Loyola/IDG




According to Apple, iOS 27 supports iPhones back to the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features require newer hardware.
Support for iOS 27 does not mean every device gets every feature. Apple Intelligence requires an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 or later, while the most advanced on-device AI models require an iPhone 17 Pro or iPhone Air. On iPad, Apple Intelligence requires an M1-class model or the A17 Pro iPad mini, while the newest on-device models require an M4 iPad with at least 12GB of RAM.
There had been speculation that the iPhone 11 series and iPhone SE 2 would miss out on iOS 27 after leaker Instant Digital claimed on Weibo that the 2019 iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max, along with the 2020 iPhone SE 2, would no longer be supported. That prediction proved incorrect, giving those models at least one more year of software support.
However, the iPhone 11 generation is nearing the end of its support life. As we explain in our guide to how long Apple supports iPhones, the iPhone 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max have already been added to Apple’s Vintage iPhone list.
The iOS 27 compatibility list is:
iPhone 17e (launched in 2026) 
iPhone 17, 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max (launched in 2025)
iPhone Air (launched in 2025)
iPhone 16e (launched in 2025)
iPhone 16 / 16 Plus and iPhone 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max (launched in 2024)
iPhone 15 / 15 Plus and iPhone 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max (launched in 2023)
iPhone 14 / 14 Plus / 14 Pro / 14 Pro Max (launched in 2022)
iPhone SE 3 (launched in 2022)
iPhone 13 / 13 mini / 13 Pro / 13 Pro Max (launched in 2021)
iPhone 12 / 12 mini / 12 Pro / 12 Pro Max (launched in 2020)
iPhone SE 2 (launched in 2020)
iPhone 11 / 11 Pro / 11 Pro Max (launched in 2019)
The main dividing line for Apple Intelligence remains the iPhone 15 Pro generation: the standard iPhone 15 and all older models can run iOS 27, but they do not support Apple Intelligence.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
When is iOS 27 coming out? 
Apple hasn’t confirmed exactly when iOS 27 will be available to install, but it usually launches to the general public in September, or at the latest October.
Once iOS 27 launches Apple will likely continue beta development to test new features that weren’t available at launch.





2.
Should I install the iOS 27 beta?
Installing a beta lets you test new features ahead of release, so you may be keen to install the beta on your iPhone, but before you do beware of the risks. 
For most users, the recommendation is simple: don’t install the beta. Pre-release software can be unstable. Bugs, performance issues, and app incompatibility are common as Apple uses the beta period to identify and fix problems before the final version launches.
If, despite our warnings, you’re still eager to try the new features, be sure to make a backup of all important information, passwords, and so on.
If you want to uninstall the iOS 27 beta read: How to remove an iOS beta from your iPhone.





3.
Which iPhones get iOS 27?
The iPhone 11 and iPhone SE 2 and newer get iOS 27. However, the new Siri voices feature requires iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro or newer.





4.
Which iPhones will get Siri AI and Apple Intelligence in iOS 27?
The only iPhones that can run Siri AI are the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max and any newer generation. If you have an iPhone 15 then you won’t get Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.

title: Apple to Mac developers: It’s time to let go of Intel
content:
Macworld





When Apple introduced its M-series chips, it also marked the beginning of the end for software written for Intel Macs. It’s been nearly six years since then, and Apple has let developers know that they can bring Intel Mac development to a close. 
In an email to developers, Apple said:
We’re reaching out to let you know that universal macOS apps on the Mac App Store that require macOS 13 or later can now remove support for Intel-based Mac computers.
By removing support for Intel-based Mac computers, you can simplify your development and optimize your download and on-device size.
When Apple announced macOS 26 Tahoe last year, the company said it would be the last version to support Intel Macs. This new announcement takes another step toward dropping Intel altogether. A new Apple support document adds this vital bit of information:
macOS 27: Final release to support Rosetta — Intel-only apps will no longer run on Mac computers with Apple silicon after this update.
Now it’s up to developers to determine when to stop with Intel code. App designers will need to determine how many of their users still use Intel Macs before they can drop development, which means that some will need to continue to support Intel for a while. If you use an Intel app, reach out to the app developer to find out their plans.

title: 153 million stolen driver's license scans expose a growing ID problem
content:

KrebsOnSecurity was alerted to the existence of the dark web site on August 31. Upon visiting the site, KrebsOnSecurity found the 153 million figure plausible; a blank search in Nexus returned 11.5 million pages of results, with 15 results per page.

title: Apple teams up with Yahoo Sports to frustrate MLB fans even more
content:
Macworld





It’s no secret that sports fans hate streaming. What used to be a consistent place to watch your local team play every night is now spread across several platforms, including Peacock, Netflix, Amazon, and Apple TV. It seems like every night, social media lights up with baseball fans who either can’t find or don’t want to pay to watch one of the two games being broadcast on some streaming service.
Apple seemingly understands at least one of these frustrations. Variety reports that Apple has inked a deal with Yahoo Sports to stream a pair of Friday Night Baseball games— Detroit Tigers at Cleveland Guardians on September 4, and Philadelphia Phillies at New York Mets on September 18—for free on Yahoo’s site and apps.
The only problem is that Yahoo is only airing the first two innings of each game. So if you’re a fan of the New York Mets and you excitedly stumble across the game and start watching, you’ll get cut off after about a half-hour of action. And as anyone who watches baseball will tell you, the first two innings are generally not the most exciting.
The truncated games will also have their own announcers, Jake Mintz and Jordan Shusterman, hosts of Yahoo Sports’ “Baseball Bar-B-Cast” podcast.
As part of the deal, Yahoo Sports will promote Apple TV’s Friday Night Baseball broadcasts through on-site ads, emails, social promotion, how-to-watch articles, “Daily Draw” games, and more, according to Variety. The deal also includes two MLS games featuring Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami CF squad, though those matches will be shown in their entirety.

title: iPhone Driver's License Feature in Apple Wallet Launches in Oklahoma
content:
Starting today, Oklahoma residents can add a digital version of their driver's license to the Apple Wallet app on the iPhone and Apple Watch. The digital ID can be used to display proof of identity or age at TSA checkpoints in select airports, at select businesses, and in select apps, but the number of places where it is accepted is still quite limited.


Oklahoma is the 16th state to implement support for Apple Wallet IDs in the U.S., joining Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Georgia, Hawaii, Illinois, Iowa, Maryland, Montana, New Mexico, North Dakota, Ohio, Virginia, and West Virginia. The feature is also available in Puerto Rico and works with Japan's My Number Card.

Apple has also been preparing for the feature to go live in North Carolina and Utah in the coming months, and years ago it announced that Connecticut, Kentucky, and Mississippi were committed to launching the feature at some point.

To set up the feature, open the Wallet app on the iPhone and tap on the plus sign in the top-right corner. Next, tap on Driver's License and ID Cards, select Oklahoma from the list, and follow the on-screen steps to complete the process. Then, you can present your digital ID where it is accepted without handing over your device.


You can present an Apple Wallet ID where accepted by simply tapping your iPhone or Apple Watch on an identity reader. Then, you will be able to view the specific information being requested by the TSA or business. Only after authorizing with Face ID or Touch ID is the requested identity information released from your device.

As mentioned, you do not need to unlock, show, or hand over your device to present an Apple Wallet ID in person, ensuring user privacy.

Apple Wallet IDs are generally not accepted by law enforcement, so carrying a physical ID is still legally required for traffic stops. In addition, the number of businesses that accept Apple Wallet IDs is still quite small. At least for now, Apple Wallet IDs are designed to be a convenient alternative where they are accepted.

title: Siri AI won’t be your friend, and here’s why that really matters
